questions.s:
Two sides of a right triangle have lengths 6 and 8. Which of the following could be the length of the third side?

Indicate all such lengths.
questions.e: If 6 and 8 are the legs, the hypotenuse is √(36 + 64) = 10. But 8 could itself be the hypotenuse, and then the other leg is √(64 − 36) = √28 = 2√7. Both are possible. Stopping at 10 is the trap: the problem never says which side is the hypotenuse. 2 and 14 come from subtracting or adding the sides.

questions.s: A regular octagon is formed by cutting four congruent isosceles right triangles from the corners of a square with side length 12, as shown. What is the length of a side of the octagon?
questions.e: Let s be a side of the octagon. Each cut-off triangle has hypotenuse s, so its legs are s/√2. One side of the square is leg + s + leg: s + 2(s/√2) = s(1 + √2) = 12. So s = 12/(1 + √2) = 12(√2 − 1) = 12√2 − 12 ≈ 4.97. The choice 12 − 6√2 ≈ 3.51 is the leg of a cut-off triangle, not the octagon's side, and 4 assumes the square side is split into three equal parts.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="60,15 240,15 240,195 60,195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polygon points="112.7,15 187.3,15 240,67.7 240,142.3 187.3,195 112.7,195 60,142.3 60,67.7" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><text x="150" y="214" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">12</text></svg>

questions.s: A triangle has sides of lengths 8, 15 and x, where x is an integer. If all three angles of the triangle are acute, how many values of x are possible?
questions.e: A triangle is acute when the square of its longest side is less than the sum of the squares of the other two. If x is the longest side, x² < 64 + 225 = 289, so x < 17. If 15 is the longest side, 225 < 64 + x², so x² > 161 and x ≥ 13. So x = 13, 14, 15 or 16: 4 values. The triangle inequality alone (7 < x < 23) would allow 15 values, many of which give an obtuse angle.

questions.s: In the figure, all angles are right angles. What is the perimeter of the figure?
questions.e: Slide the two edges of the notch outward: the horizontal notch edge moves up onto the top line and the vertical notch edge moves right onto the right side. The perimeter is therefore the same as that of the full 12-by-9 rectangle, 2(12 + 9) = 42, whatever the size of the notch. The data look insufficient, which tempts test takers to guess a larger number; 108 is the area of the rectangle, not a perimeter.

questions.s: Triangle T₁ is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle with area 80. Triangle T₂ is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of T₁. What is the area of T₂?
questions.e: Joining the midpoints of a triangle's sides creates a triangle similar to the original with ratio ½ (each side is half the side it is parallel to), so its area is (½)² = ¼ of the original. T₁ has area 80/4 = 20 and T₂ has area 20/4 = 5. The choices 40 and 20 halve the area at each step instead of quartering it.

questions.s: In the figure, the five line segments form a five-pointed star. What is the value of a + b + c + d + e?
questions.e: Look at the small triangle at one tip, say the one containing angle a. Each of its other two angles is an exterior angle of another triangle formed by the star, equal to the sum of two tip angles (for example b + d and c + e). Since the angles of that triangle add up to 180°, a + (b + d) + (c + e) = 180. The result holds for any such star. 36 is one tip of a regular star, and 108 is an interior angle of a regular pentagon.

questions.s:
The measure of the largest angle of a triangle is exactly 4 times the measure of the smallest angle. Which of the following could be the measure, in degrees, of the smallest angle?

Indicate all such measures.
questions.e: If the smallest angle is a, the largest is 4a and the middle one is 180 − 5a. The middle angle must lie between a and 4a: 180 − 5a ≥ a gives a ≤ 30, and 180 − 5a ≤ 4a gives a ≥ 20. So 20, 25 and 30 work (for example 20°, 80°, 80° or 30°, 30°, 120°). With 15 the middle angle would be 105°, larger than 4 × 15 = 60°; with 36 it would be 0°.

questions.s: Two pentagons are similar. Their perimeters are 15 and 25, and the area of the smaller pentagon is 27. What is the area of the larger pentagon?
questions.e: For similar figures, perimeters scale by the length ratio k = 25/15 = 5/3, and areas scale by k² = 25/9. The larger area is 27 × 25/9 = 75. The choice 45 scales the area by k instead of k², and 125 scales it by k³, which is how volumes would scale.

questions.s: In the figure, ABCD is a square and BCE is an equilateral triangle. What is the measure of angle AEB?
questions.e: AB = BC = BE, so triangle ABE is isosceles with AB = BE. Its vertex angle is ABE = 90° + 60° = 150°, so each base angle is (180 − 150)/2 = 15°. The choice 75° comes from drawing the triangle inside the square, where angle ABE would be 90 − 60 = 30°; 60° is an angle of the equilateral triangle, not of triangle ABE.

questions.s: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: In any triangle, the larger angle is opposite the longer side. Angle C is opposite AB = 7, and angle B is opposite AC = 9. Since 9 > 7, angle B is larger, whatever the length of BC. Do not try to read the angles from the figure; it is not drawn to scale.

questions.e: Taking one exterior angle at each vertex, the exterior angles of any convex polygon add up to 360°: n(180°) minus the interior sum (n − 2)(180°) is always 360°. So both quantities are 360°. The trap is to think more sides means a larger sum, which is true only for interior angles.
questions.qa: The sum of the measures of the exterior angles of a hexagon, one at each vertex
questions.qb: The sum of the measures of the exterior angles of an octagon, one at each vertex

questions.s: A triangle has sides of lengths 5, 12 and 13.
questions.e: Since 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13², the triangle is a right triangle with legs 5 and 12. Its area is ½ × 5 × 12 = 30, so the quantities are equal. Without spotting the right angle you might think the height is unknown and pick (D).

questions.s: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: A quadrilateral with four sides of length 5 is a rhombus. If its angles are right angles it is a square with area 25, but if it leans, its height is less than 5 and its area is less than 25. Both cases fit the information, so the relationship cannot be determined. The figure only looks like a slanted rhombus; it is not drawn to scale, so it cannot settle the question.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="40,180 200,180 260,60 100,60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="120" y="202" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="230" y="50" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="58" y="120" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="244" y="126" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>

questions.s: Rectangle R has a perimeter of 20 and is not a square.
questions.e: The sides add up to 10. Writing them as 5 + d and 5 − d, the area is 25 − d². Because R is not a square, d ≠ 0, so the area is always less than 25. Without the words 'not a square', the answer would be (D), since a 5-by-5 square has area exactly 25.

questions.s: Two sides of a triangle have lengths 6 and 9.
questions.e: By the triangle inequality the third side is less than 6 + 9 = 15 (and greater than 9 − 6 = 3). It can never reach 15, because then the three segments would lie flat in a line. So Quantity B is always greater.
questions.qa: The length of the third side

questions.s: The hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle has length 10.
questions.e: In an isosceles right triangle the hypotenuse is a leg times √2, so each leg is 10/√2 = 5√2. Since (5√2)² = 50 > 49 = 7², the leg is greater than 7 (about 7.07). Comparing squares avoids rounding √2 too roughly; 1.4 × 5 = 7 would wrongly suggest equality.
questions.qa: The length of one leg of the triangle

questions.s: In the figure, line ℓ is parallel to line m.
questions.e: Angles a and b lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate interior angles, and alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines are equal. The answer would be (D) only if the lines were not known to be parallel.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="60" x2="280" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="160" x2="280" y2="160" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="196.9" y1="23.7" x2="116.5" y2="196.3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="272" y="52" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">ℓ</text><text x="272" y="152" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">m</text><text x="144" y="82" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">a°</text><text x="163.4" y="152" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">b°</text></svg>

questions.s: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: x and y are same-side interior angles, and they add up to 180° only when lines ℓ and m are parallel. Nothing says the lines are parallel, and the figure is not drawn to scale, so the sum could be more than, less than or equal to 180. If the lines tilt toward each other on the right, x + y < 180; if they spread apart, x + y > 180.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="55" x2="280" y2="70" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="165" x2="280" y2="150" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="175" y1="25" x2="135" y2="200" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="272" y="58" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">ℓ</text><text x="272" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">m</text><text x="188" y="92" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text><text x="172" y="142" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y°</text></svg>

questions.s: The measures of the angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.
questions.e: The angles are 30°, 60° and 90°, so this is a 30°-60°-90° triangle with sides in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. The longest side (hypotenuse) is twice the shortest side. The trap is to assume the sides are in the same 1 : 2 : 3 ratio as the angles, which would give 3; sides are not proportional to angles.
questions.qa: The ratio of the length of the longest side to the length of the shortest side

questions.s: A square and an equilateral triangle each have a perimeter of 24.
questions.e: The square has side 6 and area 36. The triangle has side 8 and area (√3/4) × 8² = 16√3 ≈ 27.7. With equal perimeters, the figure that is 'rounder' (more sides, more regular) encloses more area, so the square wins.

questions.s: In quadrilateral ABCD, angle A and angle B are right angles.
questions.e: The four angles add up to 360°, so C + D = 180°, but nothing fixes how that 180° is split. ABCD could be a rectangle (C = D = 90°) or a right trapezoid with C = 70° and D = 110°, or the other way round. So the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: QR is opposite the 50° angle at P, and PR is opposite angle Q, which is unknown. If angle Q is 70°, then PR is the longer side; if angle Q is 30°, then QR is longer; if angle Q is 50°, they are equal. Only the angle at P is given, so the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="60,40 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="60" y="32" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">Q</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">R</text><text x="74" y="80.3" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">50°</text></svg>

questions.s: A triangle has sides of lengths 4, 5 and 6.
questions.e: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 6. Compare 6² = 36 with 4² + 5² = 41. Since 36 < 41, the angle is less than 90° (it would be exactly 90° if they were equal, and obtuse if 36 were larger). So Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The measure of the largest angle of the triangle

questions.s: The measures of the angles of a triangle are a°, b° and c°, where a > b > c.
questions.e: The three angles average 180/3 = 60°. If the largest angle a were 60 or less, all three would be at most 60 and, since they are not all equal, their sum would be less than 180. So a > 60. Picking an equilateral triangle to test is not allowed here, because the angles must be different.

questions.s: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: The area is the base 8 times the height. The height is at most the slanted side 5, and equals 5 only when the parallelogram is a rectangle. So the area is 40 for a rectangle and less than 40 otherwise. Since the figure is not drawn to scale, its angles cannot be assumed, and the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="30,180 210,180 270,70 90,70" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="120" y="202" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">8</text><text x="46" y="125" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>

questions.s: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 10 and one leg of length 6.
questions.e: The other leg is √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8, which is greater than 7. This is the 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 2. A hurried reader may add the squares (√136) or subtract the lengths (4); both are mistakes, but here the subtraction slip would flip the answer.
questions.qa: The length of the other leg

questions.s: The lengths of the sides of a triangle are integers, and the perimeter of the triangle is 12.
questions.e: Any side must be shorter than the sum of the other two, which is 12 minus that side. So each side is less than 12/2 = 6. The possible triangles are 2-5-5, 3-4-5 and 4-4-4, with longest side 5, 5 or 4. Sides 6, 5, 1 fail because 5 + 1 = 6 is not greater than 6.
questions.qa: The length of the longest side

questions.s:
In triangle ABC, D is a point on BC with BD = DC.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: Triangles ABD and ADC have equal bases BD = DC, and they share the same height: the perpendicular distance from A to line BC. So their areas are equal, whatever the shape of triangle ABC. The figure makes ABD look smaller, but it is not drawn to scale and the shape does not matter anyway.
questions.fg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="90,30 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="90" y1="30" x2="150" y2="190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="184" x2="90" y2="196" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="210" y1="184" x2="210" y2="196" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="90" y="22" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="150" y="210" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">D</text></svg>

questions.s: The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a convex polygon is 1,080°.
questions.e: From (n − 2) × 180 = 1,080, n − 2 = 6 and n = 8. A pentagon has 5 × (5 − 3)/2 = 5 diagonals. So Quantity A, 8, is greater. Count diagonals with n(n − 3)/2; using n(n − 1)/2 = 10 for the pentagon counts its sides too and would wrongly make B larger.
questions.qa: The number of sides of the polygon
questions.qb: The number of diagonals of a pentagon

questions.e: Every even number greater than 2 is divisible by 2 and so has a divisor other than 1 and itself. That leaves 2 as the only even prime, so Quantity A is 1. The quantities are equal; remember that 1 is not prime and 2 is.
questions.qa: The number of even prime numbers

questions.s: x is an integer, and −2 < x < 2.
questions.e: The possible values are x = −1, 0 and 1. For x = −1, x² = 1 is greater than x; for x = 0 or x = 1, x² = x. Since the comparison changes, the relationship cannot be determined; checking only 0 and 1 suggests "equal".
7 × 14 = 98 is the greatest two-digit multiple of 7. The least three-digit multiple is 7 × 15 = 105, and 105 − 10 = 95. Since 98 > 95, Quantity A is greater.
questions.qb: The least three-digit multiple of 7, minus 10

questions.e: 47 = 6 × 7 + 5, so Quantity A is 5. 47 = 8 × 5 + 7, so Quantity B is 7. Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The remainder when 47 is divided by 6
questions.qb: The remainder when 47 is divided by 8

questions.s: n is a positive integer, and the remainder when n is divided by 4 is 1.
questions.e: n = 4k + 1, so n² = 16k² + 8k + 1 = 8(2k² + k) + 1, which leaves remainder 1 when divided by 8. For example, 5² = 25 = 24 + 1 and 9² = 81 = 80 + 1. In fact the square of every odd integer leaves remainder 1 on division by 8. The quantities are equal.
questions.qa: The remainder when n² is divided by 8

questions.s: a and b are positive integers, and a/b = 0.35.
questions.e: 0.35 = 35/100 = 7/20 in lowest terms, so b must be a multiple of 20: a = 7 and b = 20, or a = 14 and b = 40, and so on. b = 20 makes the quantities equal, but b = 40 makes Quantity A greater. The relationship cannot be determined; assuming the fraction is in lowest terms is the trap.

questions.s: x is the least positive integer that is divisible by each of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.
questions.e: x is the least common multiple of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. Using the highest power of each prime, 2² × 3 × 5 = 60. Quantity B is greater; 120 comes from multiplying 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 and ignoring the shared factors.

questions.s: On a number line, point M is the midpoint of the segment from −8 to 14.
questions.e: The midpoint is the average of the endpoints: (−8 + 14) ÷ 2 = 3. The distance from 3 to 14 is 11, which is half the length of the segment, 22 ÷ 2. Quantity B is greater; confusing the coordinate of the midpoint with half the length is the trap.

questions.s: x and y are positive integers, and x² − y² = 15.
questions.e: x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y) = 15, and both factors are positive integers with x − y < x + y. So they are 1 and 15 (x = 8, y = 7) or 3 and 5 (x = 4, y = 1). x could be 8, making Quantity A greater, or 4, making the quantities equal. The relationship cannot be determined; finding only the pair 4 and 1 is the trap.

questions.s: n is a positive integer.
questions.e: Every divisor of n is also a divisor of 2n, and 2n itself divides 2n but not n. So 2n always has at least one more divisor than n. The count does not always double (n = 2 has 2 divisors and 4 has 3), but Quantity A is always greater.
questions.qa: The number of positive divisors of 2n
questions.qb: The number of positive divisors of n

questions.s: k is the sum of the digits of 10^25 − 1.
questions.e: 10^25 is 1 followed by 25 zeros, so 10^25 − 1 is written with 25 nines (just as 10³ − 1 = 999 has three). Its digit sum is 25 × 9 = 225. Quantity A is greater; the trap is thinking of 10^25 − 1 as a number full of zeros with a small digit sum.

questions.s: a, b and c are consecutive odd integers, and a < b < c.
questions.e: Write a = b − 2 and c = b + 2. Then c² − a² = (c − a)(c + a) = 4 × 2b = 8b. This holds for every odd b, including negative ones, so the quantities are equal. Testing 1, 3, 5 gives 24 = 8 × 3, which confirms it.

questions.s: What is the least common multiple of 8 and 14?
questions.e: 8 = 2³ and 14 = 2 × 7, so the least common multiple is 2³ × 7 = 56. 112 = 8 × 14 is a common multiple but not the least, because 8 and 14 share the factor 2. 2 is their greatest common factor.

questions.s: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.e: To test a number below 100, check divisibility by 2, 3, 5 and 7. 73 is not divisible by any of them, so it is prime. 51 = 3 × 17, 57 = 3 × 19 and 63 = 7 × 9 fail the test for 3, and 91 = 7 × 13 is the classic number that looks prime but is not.

questions.s: What is the remainder when 1,000 is divided by 13?
questions.e: 13 × 76 = 988 and 13 × 77 = 1,001, which is too big. So 1,000 = 13 × 76 + 12, and the remainder is 12. A quick check: 1,000 is 1 less than 1,001, a multiple of 13, so the remainder is 13 − 1 = 12.

questions.s: If n is an odd integer, which of the following is even?
questions.e: An odd number times an odd number is odd, so n² is odd and n² + 1 is even. n + 2 adds an even number to an odd one and stays odd; 3n and n³ are products of odd numbers; 2n − 1 is always odd. Trying n = 3 confirms it: 3² + 1 = 10.

questions.s: The sum of the integers from 1 to 50, inclusive, is 1,275. What is the sum of the integers from 51 to 100, inclusive?
questions.e: Each integer from 51 to 100 is exactly 50 more than a matching integer from 1 to 50 (51 = 1 + 50, ..., 100 = 50 + 50). There are 50 such pairs, so the new sum is 1,275 + 50 × 50 = 1,275 + 2,500 = 3,775. 2,550 doubles the first sum, and 2,500 is only the extra amount.

questions.s: How many positive integers less than 50 have exactly three positive divisors?
questions.e: A number has exactly three divisors only if it is the square of a prime p, with divisors 1, p and p². The squares of primes below 50 are 4, 9, 25 and 49, so there are 4. Forgetting 49, which is still less than 50, gives 3; including non-prime squares such as 16 gives too many.

questions.s:
x is an integer, and −3 < 2x + 1 < 6. Which of the following could be the value of x?

Indicate all such values.
questions.e: Subtract 1 from each part: −4 < 2x < 5. Divide by 2: −2 < x < 2.5. The integers in this interval are −1, 0, 1 and 2. −2 is excluded because the inequality is strict (2(−2) + 1 = −3 is not greater than −3), and 3 gives 7, which is too large.

questions.s: How many of the integers from 1 to 60, inclusive, are divisible by neither 2 nor 3?
questions.e: There are 30 multiples of 2 and 20 multiples of 3 from 1 to 60, and 10 multiples of 6 are in both groups. So 30 + 20 − 10 = 40 numbers are divisible by 2 or 3, and 60 − 40 = 20 are divisible by neither. 40 answers the opposite question, and 10 comes from subtracting the overlap twice.

questions.s: What is the least integer greater than 1 that leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by each of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?
questions.e: If n leaves remainder 1 for each divisor, then n − 1 is divisible by all of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, so n − 1 is a multiple of their least common multiple, 60. The least such n greater than 1 is 60 + 1 = 61. The number 1 itself leaves remainder 1 every time, which is why the question asks for an integer greater than 1.

questions.s: What is the greatest integer k such that 3^k is a factor of the product of all the integers from 1 to 30, inclusive?
questions.e: Count the factors of 3 contributed by the numbers 1 to 30. There are 10 multiples of 3, 3 multiples of 9 (each gives an extra 3) and 1 multiple of 27 (one more), so k = 10 + 3 + 1 = 14. Stopping after the multiples of 3 gives 10, and forgetting 27 gives 13.

questions.s: How many positive integers less than 1,000 have digits whose sum is 5?
questions.e: Write every such number with three digits, using leading zeros (5 = 005, 41 = 041). Then you need the number of ways to write 5 as a + b + c with digits a, b, c ≥ 0, which is the number of ways to place 2 dividers among 5 units: C(7, 2) = 21. Leading zeros are harmless here because the sum 0 never occurs. 15 counts only the three-digit numbers and misses one- and two-digit ones such as 5, 14 and 50.

questions.s:
n is a positive integer, and n² is divisible by 72. Which of the following must be divisors of n?

Indicate all such numbers.
questions.e: 72 = 2³ × 3². Exponents in n² are even, so n² must contain at least 2⁴ and 3², which means n contains at least 2² × 3 = 12. Since n = 12 works (144 = 72 × 2), the numbers that must divide n are the divisors of 12 in the list: 4, 6 and 12. 8, 9 and 24 fail for n = 12; 9 is the tempting one, but n needs only one factor of 3.

questions.s: How many positive divisors of 360 are not divisible by 6?
questions.e: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5 has 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 divisors. A divisor divisible by 6 has the form 6m, where m divides 360 ÷ 6 = 60, and 60 has 12 divisors. So 24 − 12 = 12 divisors are not divisible by 6. Counting only the odd divisors (6) or only those not divisible by 3 (8) misses part of the group.

36 = 2² × 3², so it has (2 + 1)(2 + 1) = 9 positive divisors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36. Listing them in pairs (1 and 36, 2 and 18, 3 and 12, 4 and 9) gives 8, plus 6 on its own because 6 × 6 = 36. Forgetting that a perfect square has one unpaired divisor leads to the wrong count of 8.
questions.qa: The number of positive divisors of 36

questions.e: The primes between 20 and 40 are 23, 29, 31 and 37, so Quantity A is 4. Numbers such as 21 (3 × 7), 27 (3 × 9), 33 (3 × 11) and 39 (3 × 13) look prime but are multiples of 3; counting one of them gives the tempting 5. Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The number of prime numbers between 20 and 40

questions.e: 48 = 2⁴ × 3 and 72 = 2³ × 3², so their greatest common factor is 2³ × 3 = 24. The least common multiple of 4 and 10 is 20, not their product 40, because they share the factor 2. Since 24 > 20, Quantity A is greater; using 40 for Quantity B would wrongly make B greater.
questions.qa: The greatest common factor of 48 and 72
questions.qb: The least common multiple of 4 and 10

questions.s: x is an even integer.
questions.e: −1 raised to an even power is always 1, because the negative factors pair up: (−1)² = 1, (−1)⁴ = 1, and so on. This also holds for x = 0, since (−1)⁰ = 1, and for negative even x, since (−1)^(−2) = 1/1 = 1. The two quantities are equal.

The square of any nonzero number is positive, so n² > 0, while n itself is negative. A positive number is always greater than a negative one, so Quantity A is greater. Trying a fraction such as n = −1/2 gives n² = 1/4, which is still greater than −1/2.
100 = 7 × 14 + 2, so the remainder in Quantity A is 2. 100 = 9 × 11 + 1, so the remainder in Quantity B is 1. Quantity A is greater; a larger divisor does not always give a larger remainder.
questions.qa: The remainder when 100 is divided by 7
questions.qb: The remainder when 100 is divided by 9

questions.s: a, b and c are consecutive integers, and a < b < c.
questions.e: Write the integers as b − 1, b and b + 1. Then a + c = (b − 1) + (b + 1) = 2b, whatever b is, including negative values and zero. The two quantities are always equal.

questions.s: k is a two-digit positive integer whose tens digit is 3.
questions.e: k can be any integer from 30 to 39. If k = 39, Quantity A is greater; if k = 31, Quantity B is greater; if k = 35, they are equal. Because different allowed values give different results, the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: On a number line, point P is at −3 and point Q is at 5.
questions.e: The distance between two points on a number line is the absolute value of the difference of their coordinates: |5 − (−3)| = 8. Adding the coordinates, 5 + (−3) = 2, is the trap that makes the quantities look equal. Since 8 > 2, Quantity A is greater.
questions.qa: The distance between P and Q

questions.s: x is an integer, and x² = x.
questions.e: x² = x means x² − x = x(x − 1) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 1. If x = 1 the quantities are equal, but if x = 0 Quantity B is greater. Dividing both sides by x loses the solution x = 0, which is why "equal" is the trap.

The multiples of 6 between 1 and 50 are 6, 12, ..., 48, which is 48 ÷ 6 = 8 numbers. The multiples of 8 between 1 and 70 are 8, 16, ..., 64, which is 64 ÷ 8 = 8 numbers. The quantities are equal, even though the ranges and divisors differ.
questions.qa: The number of multiples of 6 between 1 and 50
questions.qb: The number of multiples of 8 between 1 and 70

questions.s: p is a prime number.
questions.e: The smallest prime number is 2, so p could equal 2, making the quantities equal. But p could also be 3, 5, 7 or any larger prime, making Quantity A greater. Since both outcomes are possible, the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: m and n are odd integers.
questions.e: The sum of two odd integers is always even, for example 3 + 5 = 8 or −7 + 1 = −6. An even number leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2, so Quantity A is 0. Quantity B is greater; thinking "odd plus odd is odd" leads to the wrong choice of equal.
questions.qa: The remainder when m + n is divided by 2

questions.e: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5, so its distinct prime factors are 2, 3 and 5, whose sum is 10. Counting 2 twice (2 + 2 + 3 + 5 = 12) is the trap, but the question asks only for distinct primes. Since 10 < 12, Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The sum of the distinct prime factors of 60

questions.s: n is a positive integer that is divisible by both 4 and 6.
questions.e: A number divisible by both 4 and 6 is a multiple of their least common multiple, 12. So n could be 12, giving equal quantities, or 24, 36 and so on, making Quantity A greater. The relationship cannot be determined; picking only the smallest value, 12, is the trap.

questions.s: x < 0 < y
questions.e: x is negative and y is positive, and the product of a negative number and a positive number is negative. So xy < 0 for every allowed pair, including fractions such as x = −1/4 and y = 1/2. Quantity B is greater.
The digits of 4,086 add up to 4 + 0 + 8 + 6 = 18. The digits of 236 multiply to 2 × 3 × 6 = 36. Since 18 < 36, Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The sum of the digits of 4,086
questions.qb: The product of the digits of 236

questions.s: On a number line, point R is at 2/3 and point S is at 3/4.
questions.e: The midpoint is the average of the coordinates: (2/3 + 3/4) ÷ 2 = (8/12 + 9/12) ÷ 2 = 17/24. As a decimal, 17/24 ≈ 0.708, which is slightly more than 0.7. Quantity A is greater; the numbers are close, so convert carefully rather than estimate.
questions.qa: The coordinate of the point halfway between R and S

questions.s: The sum of three consecutive integers is 42.
questions.e: The middle integer of three consecutive integers is their average, 42 ÷ 3 = 14. The integers are 13, 14 and 15, so the greatest is 15. The quantities are equal.
questions.qa: The greatest of the three integers

questions.e: The least common multiple of 9 = 3² and 12 = 2² × 3 is 2² × 3² = 36. Quantity B is 108 ÷ 3 = 36. They are equal because, for any two positive integers, the product equals GCF × LCM, and the greatest common factor of 9 and 12 is 3.
questions.qa: The least common multiple of 9 and 12

questions.s: When the positive integer n is divided by 5, the remainder is 3.
questions.e: Adding 4 to n adds 4 to its remainder: 3 + 4 = 7, and 7 = 5 + 2, so n + 4 leaves remainder 2. For example, n = 8 gives n + 4 = 12, which leaves remainder 2. Quantity B is greater; 7 is not a valid remainder when dividing by 5.
questions.qa: The remainder when n + 4 is divided by 5

questions.s: k is an integer.
questions.e: k² + k = k(k + 1), the product of two consecutive integers. One of any two consecutive integers is even, so the product is always even and leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2. The quantities are equal for every integer k, including zero and negatives.
questions.qa: The remainder when k² + k is divided by 2

questions.e: 51 = 3 × 17 and 52 is even, so the least prime greater than 50 is 53. Working down from 60, 59 is prime, so it is the greatest prime less than 60. Since 53 < 59, Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The least prime number greater than 50
questions.qb: The greatest prime number less than 60

questions.s: a and b are numbers such that ab < 0 and a > b.
questions.e: ab < 0 means a and b have opposite signs, so one is positive and the other negative. Since a > b, a must be the positive one. Therefore a > 0, and Quantity A is greater.
The multiples of 7 from 1 to 100 are 7, 14, ..., 98, and 98 = 7 × 14. So there are exactly 14 of them, and 105 is already past 100. The quantities are equal.
questions.qa: The number of integers from 1 to 100, inclusive, that are divisible by 7

questions.s: x is a positive integer factor of 18.
questions.e: The positive factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18. If x = 9, Quantity A is greater; if x = 2, Quantity B is greater; if x = 6, they are equal. The relationship cannot be determined.
The integers between −4.5 and 3.2 are −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and 3. That is 8 integers; remember to count 0. The quantities are equal.
questions.qa: The number of integers between −4.5 and 3.2

questions.s: n is an integer.
questions.e: Among any three consecutive integers, exactly one is a multiple of 3, so their product is divisible by 3. The remainder in Quantity A is therefore always 0, even when one of the factors is 0 or negative. Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The remainder when n(n + 1)(n + 2) is divided by 3

questions.s: The units digit of the positive integer m is 7.
questions.e: The units digit of a product depends only on the units digits of the factors. Since 7 × 7 = 49, the units digit of m² is always 9, for example 17² = 289. Quantity A is 9 and Quantity B is 7, so Quantity A is greater.

questions.s: x and y are prime numbers.
questions.e: If x and y are different primes, such as 3 and 5, their greatest common factor is 1 and the quantities are equal. But nothing says the primes are different: if x = y = 7, the greatest common factor is 7, and Quantity A is greater. The relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The greatest common factor of x and y

questions.s: x is a negative number.
questions.e: An odd power keeps the sign, so x³ is negative, while an even power of a nonzero number is positive, so x² > 0. Any negative number is less than any positive number. Quantity B is greater for every negative x, including fractions such as −1/2.

For a number between 0 and 1, the reciprocal is greater than 1: for example, x = 1/4 gives 1/x = 4. Since x < 1 < 1/x, Quantity B is greater. Testing only whole numbers would miss that x must be a fraction here.
The remainder when an integer is divided by 10 is its units digit. 2^10 = 1,024, so Quantity A is 4, and 3⁴ = 81, so Quantity B is 1. Quantity A is greater.
questions.qa: The remainder when 2^10 is divided by 10
questions.qb: The remainder when 3⁴ is divided by 10

questions.s: a and b are integers, and a + b is even.
questions.e: An even sum only tells you that a and b are both even or both odd. They could be equal (a = b = 3), or a could be larger (a = 5, b = 1) or smaller (a = 2, b = 8). The relationship cannot be determined.

210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 has 4 distinct prime factors. 64 = 2⁶ is large in exponent but has only one distinct prime factor, 2. Quantity A is greater; counting the six factors of 2 in 64 would wrongly favor Quantity B.
questions.qa: The number of distinct prime factors of 210
questions.qb: The number of distinct prime factors of 64

questions.s: x is a positive multiple of 3, and y is a positive multiple of 5.
questions.e: Multiples of 3 and multiples of 5 overlap and interleave. x = 15 and y = 15 make the quantities equal, x = 30 and y = 5 make Quantity A greater, and x = 3 and y = 10 make Quantity B greater. The relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: The sum of four consecutive even integers is 60.
questions.e: Call the integers n, n + 2, n + 4 and n + 6. Their sum is 4n + 12 = 60, so n = 12. The integers are 12, 14, 16 and 18, and the quantities are equal.
questions.qa: The least of the four integers

questions.s: N is a three-digit integer whose digits are 4, 7 and 9 in some order.
questions.e: The possible values of N are 479, 497, 749, 794, 947 and 974. If N starts with 4, Quantity B is greater; if N starts with 7 or 9, Quantity A is greater. The relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: On a number line, the point for x lies to the left of the point for −2.
questions.e: Lying to the left of −2 means x < −2, so x is negative and farther from 0 than −2 is. The absolute value is the distance from 0, so |x| > 2. Quantity A is greater; comparing x itself with 2 would wrongly suggest Quantity B.

questions.s: n is an integer greater than 1, and 15 is divisible by n.
questions.e: The divisors of 15 that are greater than 1 are 3, 5 and 15. If n = 3, Quantity B is greater; if n = 5 or 15, Quantity A is greater. The relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: When the positive integer n is divided by 6, the remainder is 4.
questions.e: n = 6k + 4, so n is 4, 10, 16, 22, ... Dividing by 12 leaves remainder 4 (k even) or 10 (k odd). In those two cases the remainder when dividing by 4 is 0 (n = 12j + 4) or 2 (n = 12j + 10). Quantity A is 4 versus 0 or 10 versus 2, so A is always greater; the remainders vary, which tempts you to choose "cannot be determined", but the comparison never changes.
questions.qa: The remainder when n is divided by 12
questions.qb: The remainder when n is divided by 4

questions.s: n is a positive integer that has exactly 3 positive divisors.
questions.e: Only the square of a prime has exactly 3 divisors (1, p and p²), so n = p². Then n² = p⁴, whose divisors are 1, p, p², p³ and p⁴: exactly 5. For example, n = 4 gives n² = 16 with divisors 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The quantities are equal; doubling or squaring the count of 3 is the trap.
questions.qa: The number of positive divisors of n²

questions.s: m and n are integers such that 3m + 5n is odd and mn is even.
questions.e: 3m + 5n has the same parity as m + n, so m + n is odd: exactly one of m and n is odd. That already makes mn even, so the second condition adds nothing. m could be the odd one (m = 1, n = 2, remainders 1 and 0) or n could (m = 2, n = 1, remainders 0 and 1). The relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The remainder when m is divided by 2
questions.qb: The remainder when n is divided by 2

questions.s: The greatest common factor of the positive integers a and b is 6, and their least common multiple is 72.
questions.e: Write a = 6x and b = 6y with x and y sharing no factor. Then the LCM is 6xy = 72, so xy = 12 with x, y coprime: {1, 12} or {3, 4}. The pairs are 6 and 72 (sum 78) or 18 and 24 (sum 42). Both sums exceed 40, so Quantity A is greater; checking only one pair is not enough to rule out "cannot be determined".

questions.s: p and q are prime numbers, and p + q = 25.
questions.e: 25 is odd, and the sum of two odd numbers is even, so one of the primes must be the only even prime, 2. The other is 23, which is prime. So pq = 2 × 23 = 46, and the quantities are equal; it looks as if many pairs could work, but parity allows only one.

questions.s: S is the sum of five consecutive integers, and T is the sum of the next five consecutive integers.
questions.e: If S = a + (a + 1) + ... + (a + 4), then T = (a + 5) + (a + 6) + ... + (a + 9). Each term of T is exactly 5 more than the matching term of S, and there are 5 terms, so T − S = 5 × 5 = 25 for every starting integer a. The quantities are equal; trying to find the actual integers is unnecessary.

questions.s: A and B are digits with A > B > 0. AB denotes the two-digit integer with tens digit A and units digit B, and BA denotes the two-digit integer with tens digit B and units digit A.
questions.e: AB − BA = (10A + B) − (10B + A) = 9(A − B). Since B is at least 1 and A is at most 9, A − B is at most 8, so the difference is at most 72 (from 91 − 19). Quantity B is greater for every allowed pair; 98 − 89 = 9 shows that large digits alone do not give a large difference.

questions.s: x and y are nonzero numbers, x/y > 0, and x + y < 0.
questions.e: x/y > 0 means x and y have the same sign, and a negative sum means both are negative. The product of two negative numbers is positive, so xy > 0 > x + y. Quantity A is greater, even for small fractions such as x = y = −1/2, where xy = 1/4 and x + y = −1.

For x between −1 and 0, cubing keeps the sign negative but shrinks the size: x = −1/2 gives x³ = −1/8. A negative number closer to 0 is greater, so x³ > x. Quantity A is greater; the habit "powers make numbers bigger" fails both for fractions and for negatives.

questions.s: n is a positive integer, and n³ is divisible by 72.
questions.e: 72 = 2³ × 3². For n³ to contain 2³, n needs at least one factor of 2; for n³ to contain 3², n needs at least one factor of 3, because n³ then has 3³. So the least n is 2 × 3 = 6, and 6³ = 216 = 72 × 3. Quantity B is greater; 12 is what you get by requiring 2² in n, which is more than needed.
questions.qa: The least possible value of n

questions.e: Remainders of powers repeat. Powers of 7 leave remainders 2, 4, 3, 1, ... when divided by 5, in a cycle of 4; since 41 = 4 × 10 + 1, Quantity A is 2. Powers of 3 leave 3, 4, 2, 1, ...; since 22 = 4 × 5 + 2, Quantity B is 4. Quantity B is greater.
questions.qa: The remainder when 7^41 is divided by 5
questions.qb: The remainder when 3^22 is divided by 5

questions.s: k is the product of all the integers from 1 to 10, inclusive.
questions.e: Count factors of 2 in 1 × 2 × ... × 10: there are 5 multiples of 2, 2 multiples of 4 and 1 multiple of 8, so m = 5 + 2 + 1 = 8. Count factors of 3: 3 multiples of 3 and 1 multiple of 9, so t = 3 + 1 = 4 and 2t = 8. The quantities are equal; counting only the multiples of 2 gives 5 and makes B look greater.
questions.qa: The greatest integer m such that 2^m is a factor of k
questions.qb: 2t, where t is the greatest integer such that 3^t is a factor of k

questions.s: x is the product of three consecutive positive integers.
questions.e: 1 × 2 × 3 = 6 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4 and remainder 1 when divided by 5, so Quantity A is greater. 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 leaves remainder 0 when divided by 4 and remainder 4 when divided by 5, so Quantity B is greater. The product is always divisible by 6, but that fixes neither remainder, so the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The remainder when x is divided by 4
questions.qb: The remainder when x is divided by 5

questions.s: p is a prime number greater than 3.
questions.e: A prime greater than 3 is odd and not a multiple of 3, so it has the form 6k + 1 or 6k − 1. Then p² = 36k² ± 12k + 1, which is 1 more than a multiple of 12. For example, 5² = 25 = 24 + 1 and 7² = 49 = 48 + 1. The quantities are always equal.
questions.qa: The remainder when p² is divided by 12

questions.s: n is a positive integer.
questions.e: Units digits of powers of 4 alternate 4, 6, 4, 6, ..., and those of powers of 9 alternate 9, 1, 9, 1, ... For odd n, Quantity A is 4 and Quantity B is 9, so B is greater; for even n, A is 6 and B is 1, so A is greater. The relationship cannot be determined; testing only n = 1 suggests B.

|x − 3| < 2 says x is within 2 of 3 on the number line, so 1 < x < 5. |y + 1| < 2 says y is within 2 of −1, so −3 < y < 1. Every allowed x is greater than 1 and every allowed y is less than 1, so x > y always. Quantity A is greater; the intervals touch at 1 but neither includes it.

questions.s: n is a positive integer.
questions.e: Any common factor of n and n + 6 also divides their difference, 6, so the greatest common factor is 1, 2, 3 or 6. If n = 6 it is 6 and the quantities are equal; if n = 1 it is 1 and Quantity B is greater. The relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The greatest common factor of n and n + 6

questions.e: Below 100 there are 33 multiples of 3 and 19 multiples of 5, but the 6 multiples of 15 are counted twice, so 33 + 19 − 6 = 46 numbers are multiples of 3 or 5. The other 99 − 46 = 53 are multiples of neither. Quantity B is greater; forgetting to subtract the overlap gives 52 for A and wrongly makes A greater.
questions.qa: The number of positive integers less than 100 that are multiples of 3 or 5
questions.qb: The number of positive integers less than 100 that are multiples of neither 3 nor 5

questions.s: x, y and z are integers, x < y < z, and x + y + z = 0.
questions.e: The average of the three integers is 0, but the middle one need not be 0. With −1, 0 and 1, y = 0; with −3, 1 and 2, y = 1; with −2, −1 and 3, y = −1. The relationship cannot be determined; assuming the numbers are symmetric about 0 is the trap.
p² < 200 means p ≤ 14, since 14² = 196 and 15² = 225. The primes up to 14 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13, so Quantity A is 6. Quantity B is greater; counting 1 as a prime would give 7.
questions.qa: The number of prime numbers p such that p² < 200

questions.s: A florist has 84 roses and 126 tulips. She wants to make identical bouquets, each with the same number of roses and the same number of tulips, using all of the flowers. What is the greatest number of bouquets she can make?
questions.e: The number of bouquets must divide both 84 and 126, so the greatest possible number is their greatest common factor. 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 126 = 2 × 3² × 7, so the GCF is 2 × 3 × 7 = 42, giving bouquets of 2 roses and 3 tulips. 252 is the least common multiple, which answers a different question.

questions.s: Two shuttle buses leave a terminal together at 7:00 a.m. One bus returns to the terminal every 18 minutes and the other every 24 minutes. At what time will the two buses next be at the terminal at the same time?
questions.e: The buses meet again after the least common multiple of 18 and 24 minutes. 18 = 2 × 3² and 24 = 2³ × 3, so the LCM is 2³ × 3² = 72 minutes, and 7:00 a.m. plus 1 hour 12 minutes is 8:12 a.m. Adding the two intervals gives 7:42 a.m., and multiplying them gives 432 minutes, or 2:12 p.m.; both are common slips.

questions.s: When the positive integer n is divided by 7, the remainder is 5. What is the remainder when 3n + 4 is divided by 7?
questions.e: Write n = 7k + 5. Then 3n + 4 = 21k + 15 + 4 = 21k + 19, and 19 = 14 + 5, so the remainder is 5. Checking with n = 5 gives 3n + 4 = 19, which also leaves 5. Answering 19 forgets that a remainder must be less than the divisor 7.

questions.s: What is the sum of all the prime numbers between 30 and 50?
questions.e: The primes between 30 and 50 are 31, 37, 41, 43 and 47, and their sum is 199. Check the odd numbers that are not multiples of 5: 33 = 3 × 11, 39 = 3 × 13 and 49 = 7 × 7 are not prime. Counting 39 or 49 as prime gives 238 or 248.

questions.s: How many positive integers less than 200 are divisible by both 6 and 8?
questions.e: A number divisible by both 6 and 8 is a multiple of their least common multiple, 24 (not 48, because 6 and 8 share a factor of 2). The multiples of 24 below 200 are 24, 48, ..., 192, and 192 = 24 × 8, so there are 8 of them. Using 12 as the LCM gives 16, and counting multiples of 6 or of 8 gives the larger choices.

questions.s: If x and y are integers and x + 2y is odd, which of the following must be odd?
questions.e: 2y is always even, so x + 2y is odd exactly when x is odd; y can be anything. Then 3x is odd and 4y is even, so 3x + 4y is odd. x − 1 is even, and xy, x + y and x + y + 1 depend on whether y is odd or even.

questions.s:
Which of the following integers have an odd number of positive divisors?

Indicate all such integers.
questions.e: Divisors come in pairs d and n/d, and a pair collapses to one divisor only when d × d = n. So a number has an odd number of divisors exactly when it is a perfect square. 16, 36 and 81 are squares (5, 9 and 5 divisors); 24, 50 and 98 are not, even though 50 = 2 × 5² and 98 = 2 × 7² contain squares.

questions.s: The sum of five consecutive odd integers is 115. What is the greatest of these integers?
questions.e: For consecutive odd integers the middle one equals the average, 115 ÷ 5 = 23. The integers are 19, 21, 23, 25 and 27, so the greatest is 27. 23 is the middle value, and 25 comes from stepping by 1 instead of 2.

questions.s: How many three-digit positive integers have digits whose sum is 4?
questions.e: The hundreds digit is 1, 2, 3 or 4. With hundreds digit 1 the other two digits sum to 3 (03, 12, 21, 30: 4 ways); with 2 they sum to 2 (3 ways); with 3 they sum to 1 (2 ways); with 4 they are 00 (1 way). The total is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10. Forgetting numbers with a 0 digit, such as 103 or 400, gives 6.

questions.s: On a number line, point P is at −7 and point Q is at 11. Point R lies between P and Q and is twice as far from P as it is from Q. What is the coordinate of R?
questions.e: PQ = 11 − (−7) = 18. R splits PQ in the ratio 2 : 1, so PR = 12 and RQ = 6, and R = −7 + 12 = 5. The midpoint is 2, and −1 is the point twice as far from Q as from P; 12 is the distance PR, not a coordinate.

questions.s: If a < 0 < b, which of the following must be negative?
questions.e: a − b is a negative number minus a positive number, which moves further left on the number line, so it is always negative. b − a is its opposite and always positive; a²b and −ab are both positive. a + b is negative only when |a| > |b|, so it need not be negative.

questions.s: The product of two positive integers is 540, and their greatest common factor is 6. What is their least common multiple?
questions.e: For any two positive integers, GCF × LCM = product of the numbers. So the LCM is 540 ÷ 6 = 90. One such pair is 18 and 30: their product is 540, their GCF is 6 and their LCM is 90.

questions.s: What is the remainder when 2^50 is divided by 7?
questions.e: Powers of 2 leave remainders 2, 4, 1, 2, 4, 1, ... when divided by 7, a cycle of length 3, because 2³ = 8 = 7 + 1. Since 50 = 3 × 16 + 2, 2^50 leaves the same remainder as 2², which is 4. Using the cycle position 50 ÷ 3 → remainder 2 as the answer itself gives the trap choice 2.

questions.s: If 2^a × 3^b × 5^c = 3,600, where a, b and c are positive integers, what is the value of a + b + c?
questions.e: 3,600 = 36 × 100 = (2² × 3²) × (2² × 5²) = 2⁴ × 3² × 5². So a = 4, b = 2 and c = 2, and a + b + c = 8. 45 is the number of divisors of 3,600, (4 + 1)(2 + 1)(2 + 1), which answers a different question.

questions.s:
The positive integer n is divisible by both 12 and 18. Which of the following must also be divisors of n?

Indicate all such numbers.
questions.e: n must be a multiple of the least common multiple of 12 and 18, which is 36 = 2² × 3², and n = 36 itself is possible. So the numbers that must divide n are exactly the divisors of 36: 4, 9, 12 and 36. 8 and 24 need 2³, which 36 does not contain, so they fail when n = 36.

questions.s: How many positive integers are factors of 200?
questions.e: 200 = 2³ × 5². A factor uses 2 to a power from 0 to 3 (4 choices) and 5 to a power from 0 to 2 (3 choices), so there are 4 × 3 = 12 factors. Multiplying the exponents themselves (3 × 2 = 6) or adding them (5) forgets the choice of power 0.

questions.s: If −3 ≤ x ≤ 2 and −1 ≤ y ≤ 4, what is the greatest possible value of y − x?
questions.e: To make y − x as large as possible, make y as large as possible and x as small as possible: y = 4 and x = −3. Then y − x = 4 − (−3) = 7. Taking both largest values gives 4 − 2 = 2, the most common slip.

questions.s: The average (arithmetic mean) of seven consecutive integers is 12. What is the product of the least and the greatest of these integers?
questions.e: For an odd number of consecutive integers, the average is the middle integer, so the integers are 9 through 15. The product of the least and greatest is 9 × 15 = 135. 144 = 12 × 12 squares the average, and 132 = 11 × 12 or 165 = 11 × 15 come from miscounting the integers on one side of 12.

questions.s: How many four-digit positive integers have thousands digit 3 and four digits that are all odd and all different?
questions.e: The thousands digit is 3, so the other three digits come from the remaining odd digits 1, 5, 7 and 9, with no repeats. There are 4 choices for the hundreds digit, 3 for the tens and 2 for the units: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24. Allowing repeats would give 4³ = 64.

questions.s: Lena packs 250 eggs into cartons that hold 12 eggs each, filling as many cartons as she can. How many more eggs would she need to fill one more carton?
questions.e: 250 = 12 × 20 + 10, so she fills 20 cartons and has 10 eggs left over. The next carton needs 12 − 10 = 2 more eggs. Choosing 10 gives the remainder itself, and 20 is the number of full cartons.

questions.s: If n is an integer, which of the following must be even?
questions.e: n² + n = n(n + 1) is the product of two consecutive integers, one of which is even, so it is always even. 2n + 1 is always odd, and n² + 1, 3n + 1 and n³ change parity depending on whether n is odd or even. For instance, n = 2 makes n² + 1 = 5 odd.

questions.s:
For which of the following values of k is 2^k − 1 a prime number?

Indicate all such values.
questions.e: The values are 2² − 1 = 3, 2³ − 1 = 7, 2⁴ − 1 = 15, 2⁵ − 1 = 31, 2⁶ − 1 = 63 and 2⁷ − 1 = 127. Of these, 3, 7, 31 and 127 are prime, while 15 = 3 × 5 and 63 = 7 × 9. When k is composite, 2^k − 1 factors, so k = 4 and k = 6 fail; but a prime k is not always enough in general, so each value must be checked.

questions.s: The least common multiple of 12, 15 and k is 180. Which of the following could be the value of k?
questions.e: lcm(12, 15) = 60 = 2² × 3 × 5, and 180 = 2² × 3² × 5, so k must supply the factor 3² and must not add any other power. 36 = 2² × 3² works: lcm(12, 15, 36) = 180. 10 leaves the LCM at 60, 8 and 24 bring in 2³ (LCM 120), and 27 brings in 3³ (LCM 540).

questions.s: The four-digit integer 52d6, where d is the tens digit, is divisible by 12. What is the value of d?
questions.e: A number is divisible by 12 when it is divisible by both 3 and 4. Divisible by 3: 5 + 2 + d + 6 = 13 + d must be a multiple of 3, so d is 2, 5 or 8. Divisible by 4: the last two digits d6 must be a multiple of 4, which needs d odd (16, 36, 56, 76, 96). Only d = 5 does both; 2 and 8 pass only the test for 3.

questions.s: If x and y are integers such that −5 ≤ x ≤ 3 and −2 ≤ y ≤ 6, what is the least possible value of xy?
questions.e: A negative product needs opposite signs, so check the two corners: x = −5 with y = 6 gives −30, and x = 3 with y = −2 gives −6. The least value is −30. Multiplying the two smallest values, (−5)(−2) = 10, gives a positive number, which is the trap.

questions.s: How many integers are there from −14 to 27, inclusive?
questions.e: The number of integers from a to b inclusive is b − a + 1 = 27 − (−14) + 1 = 42. Equivalently, there are 14 negative integers, 27 positive integers and zero. Forgetting the "+ 1", or forgetting zero, gives 41.

questions.s: What is the units digit of 7^23?
questions.e: The units digits of powers of 7 cycle through 7, 9, 3, 1 in a cycle of length 4. Since 23 = 4 × 5 + 3, 7^23 has the same units digit as 7³ = 343, which is 3. Ending the count one place too late gives 1, the units digit of 7⁴.

questions.s:
On a number line, x is closer to 2 than it is to −4, and x < 0. Which of the following could be the value of x?

Indicate all such values.
questions.e: The point equally far from 2 and −4 is their midpoint, (2 + (−4)) ÷ 2 = −1. Points to the right of −1 are closer to 2, so −1 < x < 0. Only −0.8 and −0.2 qualify: −1 is exactly as far from both, and 0.5 is closer to 2 but not negative.

questions.s: What is the greatest prime factor of 2^10 − 1?
questions.e: 2^10 − 1 = (2⁵ − 1)(2⁵ + 1) = 31 × 33 = 31 × 3 × 11. So the prime factors are 3, 11 and 31, and the greatest is 31. 33, 93 and 341 (= 11 × 31) are factors, but none of them is prime.

questions.s: When the positive integer n is divided by 12, the remainder is 7. What is the remainder when n is divided by 6?
questions.e: n = 12k + 7 = 6(2k + 1) + 1, so dividing by 6 leaves remainder 1. For example, n = 19 = 6 × 3 + 1. The choice 7 keeps the original remainder, but a remainder on division by 6 must be less than 6.

questions.s: What is the greatest common factor of 2⁴ × 3² × 7 and 2² × 3⁵ × 5?
questions.e: The greatest common factor takes each prime the numbers share, to the smaller of its two exponents. They share 2 (exponents 4 and 2) and 3 (exponents 2 and 5), while 7 and 5 each appear in only one number. So the GCF is 2² × 3² = 36. Taking the larger exponents would give part of the least common multiple instead.

questions.s: If a, b and c are integers, a is odd and b is even, which of the following must be odd?
questions.e: Because b is even, bc is even whatever c is, and odd + even is odd, so a + bc is always odd. abc is always even. ab + c, a + b + c and a(b + c) depend on whether c is odd or even, since nothing is known about c.

questions.s:
Which of the following must be a divisor of the product of any three consecutive positive integers?

Indicate all such numbers.
questions.e: Any three consecutive integers include at least one even number and exactly one multiple of 3, so the product is always divisible by 2, 3 and therefore 6. 4, 5 and 9 can fail: 1 × 2 × 3 = 6 is not divisible by 4, 5 or 9. Many products, such as 2 × 3 × 4 = 24, are divisible by 4, which is why 4 is tempting.

questions.s: The tens digit of a two-digit integer is 3 more than its units digit. The sum of the integer and the integer formed by reversing its digits is 121. What is the integer?
questions.e: If the digits are a (tens) and b (units), the sum is (10a + b) + (10b + a) = 11(a + b) = 121, so a + b = 11. With a − b = 3, a = 7 and b = 4, so the integer is 74. 47 has the right digits in the wrong order: its tens digit is 3 less than its units digit.

questions.s: If xy < 0 and yz > 0, which of the following must be true?
questions.e: xy < 0 means x and y have opposite signs, and yz > 0 means y and z have the same sign. So x and z have opposite signs, and xz < 0. The actual signs are unknown: x = 1, y = −1, z = −2 and x = −1, y = 1, z = 2 both work, so the other choices can fail.

questions.s: Which of the following is the product of three different prime numbers?
questions.e: 130 = 2 × 5 × 13, the product of three different primes. The others repeat a prime: 135 = 3³ × 5, 147 = 3 × 7², 150 = 2 × 3 × 5² and 196 = 2² × 7². 150 is tempting because its distinct primes are 2, 3 and 5, but the extra 5 makes it a product of four primes.

questions.s: How many multiples of 7 are there between 100 and 300?
questions.e: The first multiple of 7 above 100 is 105 = 7 × 15, and the last below 300 is 294 = 7 × 42. So the multiples are 7 × 15 through 7 × 42, which is 42 − 15 + 1 = 28 numbers. Dividing 200 by 7 and rounding gives 29, which overcounts.

questions.s: Which of the following numbers lies between 3/8 and 4/9 on the number line?
questions.e: 3/8 = 0.375 and 4/9 ≈ 0.444. Among the choices, 3/7 ≈ 0.429 is the only one in that interval; 4/11 ≈ 0.364 is just below 3/8 and 5/11 ≈ 0.455 is just above 4/9. Cross-multiplying confirms it: 3 × 7 = 21 < 24 = 8 × 3, so 3/8 < 3/7, and 3 × 9 = 27 < 28 = 7 × 4, so 3/7 < 4/9.

questions.s:
When the positive integer n is divided by 4, the remainder is 3. Which of the following could be the remainder when n is divided by 8?

Indicate all such remainders.
questions.e: n is one of 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, ... Dividing these by 8 gives remainders 3, 7, 3, 7, ..., because n is either 8k + 3 or 8k + 7. So only 3 and 7 are possible. Even remainders are impossible because n is odd, and 1 and 5 would give remainder 1 on division by 4.

questions.s: The greatest common factor of two positive integers is 9, and their least common multiple is 270. If one of the integers is 54, what is the other?
questions.e: GCF × LCM equals the product of the two integers, so the other integer is 9 × 270 ÷ 54 = 45. Check: 54 = 2 × 3³ and 45 = 3² × 5 share 3² = 9, and their LCM is 2 × 3³ × 5 = 270. 5 comes from 270 ÷ 54, which ignores the GCF, and 30 does not have 9 as a factor.

questions.s: A circle has a diameter of 14. What is the area of the circle?
questions.e: The radius is half the diameter, 7, so the area is π × 7² = 49π. The choice 196π uses the diameter as the radius, and 14π is the circumference.

questions.s: Which of the following points lies in quadrant IV of the xy-plane?
questions.e: Quadrants are numbered counterclockwise from the upper right. Quadrant IV is the lower right, where x > 0 and y < 0, so (3, −2) is the answer. (0, −2) lies on the y-axis, which belongs to no quadrant, and (−3, −2) is in quadrant III.

questions.s: What is the volume of the rectangular box shown, with dimensions 5, 3 and 2?
questions.e: The volume of a rectangular box is length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30. Adding the dimensions (10) or finding the area of one face (15) are the usual slips.

questions.s: A circle has a diameter of 9.
questions.e: The radius is half the diameter: 9/2 = 4.5. The quantities are equal.

questions.s: A circle has radius 1.
questions.e: The area is π × 1² = π ≈ 3.14, which is less than 3.2. Rounding π up to 3.2 or confusing it with 22/7 ≈ 3.143 does not change the answer here, but rounding to 3.2 would wrongly suggest (C).

questions.s: What is the total surface area of a cube with edges of length 3?
questions.e: A cube has 6 square faces, each with area 3 × 3 = 9, so the surface area is 6 × 9 = 54. The choice 27 is the volume (3³), and 9 is the area of a single face.

questions.s: Points A(2, 5) and B(2, −1) are shown in the xy-plane.
questions.e: A and B have the same x-coordinate, so AB is vertical and its length is the difference of the y-coordinates: 5 − (−1) = 6, which is greater than 5. Subtracting 5 − 1 = 4 ignores the negative sign.

questions.s: A circular rug has a radius of 3 meters. What is its area, in square meters?
questions.e: Area = πr² = π × 3² = 9π square meters. The choice 36π uses the diameter 6 in place of the radius, and 18π multiplies 2 × 9 instead of squaring.

questions.s: The figure shows a square with side length 8 and a quarter circle centered at the lower left corner of the square with radius 8. What is the area of the shaded region?
questions.e: The quarter circle has area ¼ × π × 8² = 16π, and the square has area 64. The shaded region is what is left: 64 − 16π ≈ 13.7. The choice 64 − 4π uses the radius 4, and 64 − 8π takes half instead of a quarter of the circle.

questions.s:
Which of the following points in the xy-plane are at a distance of exactly 5 from the point (1, 1)?

Indicate all such points.
questions.e: Check whether (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 25. (4, 5): 9 + 16 = 25. (−2, −3): 9 + 16 = 25. (−4, 1): 25 + 0 = 25. (6, 2) gives 26, (1, −5) gives 36 and (3, 6) gives 29, so they are not at distance 5. The 3-4-5 pattern is a quick way to spot the right points.

questions.s: A line in the xy-plane passes through the points (0, 3) and (k, 0), where k ≠ 0.
questions.e: The slope is (0 − 3)/(k − 0) = −3/k. If k = 3 the slope is −1; if k = 6 it is −1/2 (greater than −1); if k = 1 it is −3 (less than −1); and if k is negative the slope is positive. So the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: In the figure, O is the center of the circle and angle ACB measures 40°.
questions.e: The central angle AOB and the inscribed angle ACB intercept the same arc AB, and a central angle is twice the inscribed angle: x = 2 × 40 = 80. Since 80 < 85, B is greater. Halving instead of doubling gives 20, which leads to the same answer here only by luck.

questions.s: A cube-shaped container with inside edge 6 inches is full of water. All the water is poured into an empty cylindrical container with inside radius 3 inches, and none spills. How deep, in inches, is the water in the cylinder?
questions.e: The water's volume is 6³ = 216 cubic inches. In the cylinder it fills π × 3² × h = 9πh, so h = 216/(9π) = 24/π ≈ 7.6 inches. The choice 6/π uses the diameter 6 as the radius (216/(36π)), and 12/π divides by 18π, the area 2πr instead of πr².

questions.s: A sector of a circle with radius 6 has an area of 12π. What is the measure, in degrees, of the central angle of the sector?
questions.e: The whole circle has area π × 6² = 36π. The sector is 12π/36π = 1/3 of the circle, so its central angle is 1/3 of 360°, which is 120°. Comparing the sector with the circumference (12π) instead of the area would wrongly give 360°.

questions.s: In the xy-plane, a circle has center (2, 3) and radius 4.
questions.e: The center is 3 units above the x-axis and the radius is 4, which is more than 3, so the circle crosses the x-axis at exactly 2 points. A circle and a line can meet in at most 2 points, so Quantity A can never reach 3.
questions.qa: The number of points at which the circle intersects the x-axis

questions.s: What is the area of the parallelogram shown in the xy-plane, with vertices O(0, 0), (4, 0), (5, 3) and (1, 3)?
questions.e: The base along the x-axis has length 4, and the height is the vertical distance between the parallel sides, 3. Area = base × height = 4 × 3 = 12. The choice 6 halves it as if it were a triangle, and 15 multiplies 5 × 3, using an x-coordinate as the base.

questions.s: Cylinder X has radius 4 and height 2. Cylinder Y has radius 2 and height 8.
questions.e: X: π × 4² × 2 = 32π. Y: π × 2² × 8 = 32π. They are equal: halving the radius divides the volume by 4, which the fourfold height exactly makes up for. Squaring the height instead of the radius (π × 4 × 2² against π × 2 × 8²) is a common slip that would make Y look far larger.

questions.s: A circle is inscribed in a square, and the square is inscribed in a larger circle. What is the ratio of the area of the larger circle to the area of the smaller circle?
questions.e: If the square has side 2, the small circle has radius 1 (half the side) and the large circle has radius √2 (half the diagonal 2√2). The areas are in the ratio (√2)² : 1² = 2 : 1. The choice √2 : 1 is the ratio of the radii, not the areas.

questions.s:
Line ℓ in the xy-plane passes through the point (2, 3) and does not pass through quadrant III. Which of the following could be the slope of ℓ?

Indicate all such slopes.
questions.e: The line is y = m(x − 2) + 3. If m > 0, then far enough to the left (x very negative) y becomes negative too, so the line enters quadrant III, however small m is (for m = 1/4 that happens once x < −10). If m = 0 the line is y = 3, and if m < 0, then for every x < 0, y = m(x − 2) + 3 > 3 > 0. So exactly the slopes −3, −1/2 and 0 work.

questions.s: A square and an equilateral triangle are each inscribed in a circle with radius r.
questions.e: The square's diagonal is the diameter 2r, so its area is (2r)²/2 = 2r². The triangle's side is r√3 (its height is 1.5r, since the center is two thirds of the way down from a vertex), so its area is (√3/4)(3r²) ≈ 1.30r². The square is larger for every r.

questions.s:
The point (a, b) lies on the circle x² + y² = 25 in quadrant II, as shown.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.e: In quadrant II, a < 0 < b, and a² + b² = 25. If the point is (−3, 4), a + b = 1 > 0; if it is (−4, 3), a + b = −1 < 0; and at (−5/√2, 5/√2) the sum is 0. Since the figure is not drawn to scale, the position of the point cannot be read from it, so the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s: Three faces of a rectangular box that meet at one corner have areas 12, 15 and 20.
questions.e: If the edges are l, w and h, then lw = 12, wh = 15 and lh = 20. Multiplying, (lwh)² = 12 × 15 × 20 = 3,600, so lwh = 60. (The edges are 4, 3 and 5.) Multiplying the three areas without taking the square root gives 3,600, and adding them gives 47; neither is the volume.

questions.s: Two circles, each with radius 3, have centers P and Q, and each circle passes through the center of the other. What is the area of the shaded region common to both circles?
questions.e: Join P and Q to the two intersection points: all four segments are radii of length 3, and PQ = 3, so they form two equilateral triangles and each center sees the shaded region under a 120° angle. The part of the region on one side of the common chord is a 120° sector (area 9π/3 = 3π) minus a triangle with sides 3, 3 and 3√3 (area 9√3/4). Doubling gives 6π − 9√3/2. The choice 3π − 9√3/4 is only half the region.

questions.s: In the xy-plane, how many points with integer coordinates lie on the circle x² + y² = 25?
questions.e: We need integer pairs with x² + y² = 25. The four axis points (±5, 0) and (0, ±5) work, and so do all sign combinations of (3, 4) and (4, 3): (±3, ±4) and (±4, ±3), 8 more. Total 4 + 8 = 12. Counting only the first quadrant (3, 4) and (4, 3), or forgetting the axis points, gives too few.

questions.s: A closed cylindrical can, shown, has a volume of 54π cubic inches, and its height h equals its diameter d. What is the total surface area of the can, in square inches?
questions.e: With h = 2r, the volume is πr²(2r) = 2πr³ = 54π, so r³ = 27 and r = 3, h = 6. The two circular ends have area 2 × 9π = 18π and the curved side has area 2πrh = 2π × 3 × 6 = 36π. Total: 54π. The choice 36π is only the curved surface, and 45π counts one end.

questions.s: The circumference of a circle is 10π. What is the area of the circle?
questions.e: Circumference = 2πr = 10π gives r = 5, so the area is πr² = 25π. The choice 100π uses the diameter 10 as the radius, and 10π repeats the circumference.

questions.s: In the circle with center O shown, the radius is 10 and angle AOB measures 72°. What is the length of minor arc AB?
questions.e: An arc is the same fraction of the circumference as its central angle is of 360°. Here 72/360 = 1/5, and the circumference is 2π × 10 = 20π, so the arc is 20π/5 = 4π. The choice 20π is the whole circumference (and also the sector's area, (1/5) × 100π), not the arc length.

questions.s: The rectangular box shown has length 12, width 4 and height 3. What is the length of a diagonal of the box joining two opposite corners (shown as a dashed segment)?
questions.e: First find the diagonal of the 12-by-4 base: √(144 + 16) = √160. That segment and the height 3 are the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the box's diagonal: √(160 + 9) = √169 = 13. In one step: √(12² + 4² + 3²) = 13. Using only two of the dimensions gives a face diagonal, which is shorter.

questions.s: What is the volume of the right circular cylinder shown, which has radius 3 and height 8?
questions.e: Volume = πr²h = π × 3² × 8 = 72π. The choice 48π is the curved (lateral) surface area 2πrh, 66π is the total surface area 2πr² + 2πrh, and 288π uses the diameter 6 in place of the radius.

questions.s: In the figure, O is the center of the circle and angle AOB measures 110°. What is the measure of angle ACB?
questions.e: Angle ACB is an inscribed angle that intercepts the same arc AB as the central angle AOB, so it is half as large: 110/2 = 55°. The choice 125° is half of the other arc (360 − 110 = 250), which would apply only if C were on minor arc AB; 220° doubles instead of halving.

questions.s: In the xy-plane, what is the distance between the points (−2, 3) and (4, −5)?
questions.e: The horizontal change is 4 − (−2) = 6 and the vertical change is −5 − 3 = −8, so the distance is √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10. The choice 14 adds the two changes (walking along the grid), and 2√2 comes from a sign slip, using 4 − 2 and −5 + 3.

questions.s: In the xy-plane, what is the midpoint of the segment joining (1, 7) and (9, −3)?
questions.e: The midpoint averages the coordinates: ((1 + 9)/2, (7 + (−3))/2) = (5, 2). The choice (4, −5) halves the differences instead of averaging, (8, −10) is the full difference, and (10, 4) adds without dividing by 2.

questions.s:
Line ℓ in the xy-plane has slope 2 and passes through the point (1, 3). Which of the following points lie on ℓ?

Indicate all such points.
questions.e: The equation of ℓ is y − 3 = 2(x − 1), or y = 2x + 1. Test each point: (0, 1), (−1, −1) and (5, 11) satisfy it. (2, 4), (3, 6) and (−2, −5) fit the line y = 2x through the origin, which is the trap of forgetting the intercept.

questions.s: A square is inscribed in a circle with center O and radius 5, as shown. What is the area of the shaded region?
questions.e: The diagonal of the square is a diameter, 10, so the square's area is 10²/2 = 50 (or side 5√2 squared). The shaded region is the circle minus the square: 25π − 50 ≈ 28.5. The choice 25π − 25 takes the square's side to be 5, the radius, rather than 5√2.

questions.s: The total surface area of a cube is 150 square centimeters. What is the volume of the cube, in cubic centimeters?
questions.e: A cube has 6 equal square faces, so each face has area 150/6 = 25 and each edge is 5. The volume is 5³ = 125. A common slip is to take the edge as √150 or to divide by 4 faces instead of 6.

questions.s: What is the perimeter of a semicircular region with radius 6?
questions.e: The boundary is half the circle's circumference plus the straight diameter: ½ × 2π × 6 + 12 = 6π + 12. The choice 6π leaves out the diameter, and 6π + 6 adds the radius instead of the diameter.

questions.s: In the figure, line segment PA is tangent at A to the circle with center O. If OA = 5 and OP = 13, what is the length of PA?
questions.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so triangle OAP has a right angle at A with hypotenuse OP = 13. Then PA = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12. The choice √194 adds the squares as if OP were a leg, and 8 just subtracts the lengths.

questions.s: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (2, −1) and (6, 7) in the xy-plane?
questions.e: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x = (7 − (−1))/(6 − 2) = 8/4 = 2. The choice 1/2 divides the change in x by the change in y, and 3/4 comes from mishandling the negative: (7 − 1)/(6 + 2) = 6/8.

questions.s:
A cylindrical tank has radius 2 meters and height 3 meters. Which of the following containers have a volume greater than the volume of the tank?

Indicate all such containers.
questions.e: The tank holds π × 2² × 3 = 12π ≈ 37.7 cubic meters. The cube holds 3.5³ ≈ 42.9 and the 2-by-4-by-5 box holds 40, both more. The 3-by-3-by-4 box holds 36, the cylinder of radius 3 and height 1 holds 9π ≈ 28.3, and the cylinder of radius 1 and height 12 holds exactly 12π, which is equal, not greater.
o: a cube with edges of length 3.5 m
a rectangular box measuring 2 m by 4 m by 5 m
a cylinder with radius 3 m and height 1 m
a cylinder with radius 1 m and height 12 m
a rectangular box measuring 3 m by 3 m by 4 m

questions.s: What is the area of the triangle shown in the xy-plane, with vertices at the origin O, (6, 0) and (2, 5)?
questions.e: Use the side along the x-axis as the base: its length is 6. The height is the vertical distance from (2, 5) to the x-axis, which is 5, no matter where the top vertex sits horizontally. Area = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15. The choice 30 forgets the ½, and 7.5 halves twice.
