questions.s: The ages, in years, of five siblings are 3, 7, 11, 14 and 20.
questions.e: Range = greatest − least = 20 − 3 = 17, which is less than 18. The range uses only the two extreme values; the numbers in between do not matter.

Both sets have mean 20, but the values in X lie 10 units from the mean while those in Y lie only 1 unit away. Standard deviation measures how spread out the values are around the mean, so X has the greater standard deviation. No calculation is needed.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of set X
questions.qb: The standard deviation of set Y

questions.e: Every value equals the mean, 5, so every deviation from the mean is 0 and the standard deviation is 0. A standard deviation is never negative, and it is 0 exactly when all the values are the same.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of set P

questions.s: Class A has 10 students, whose average score is 80. Class B has 30 students, whose average score is 70.
questions.e: The combined average is a weighted average: (10 × 80 + 30 × 70)/40 = (800 + 2,100)/40 = 2,900/40 = 72.5. Because class B is three times as large, the combined average lies closer to 70. The trap is to average 80 and 70 directly, getting 75.
questions.qa: The average score of all 40 students

questions.s: The list of numbers: 3, 8, 10, 15, 21
questions.e: The median is the middle value, 10. The mean is (3 + 8 + 10 + 15 + 21)/5 = 57/5 = 11.4. So B is greater. The values above the median (15 and 21) are farther from 10 than the values below it (3 and 8), which pulls the mean up.

questions.s: In a box plot of a set of test scores, the box extends from 62 to 78, and the line inside the box is at 70.
questions.e: In a box plot the box runs from the first quartile to the third quartile, so the interquartile range is 78 − 62 = 16, which is greater than 15. The line inside the box, 70, is the median; it is not needed for the interquartile range.
questions.qa: The interquartile range of the scores

questions.s: A variable is normally distributed with mean 50 and standard deviation 5.
questions.e: A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean, so exactly half of the distribution lies above the mean and half below. The proportion above 50 is 0.5. The standard deviation affects how spread out the values are, not where the center is.
questions.qa: The proportion of the values that are greater than 50

questions.s: The mean of the numbers in set A is 20, and the mean of the numbers in set B is 30.
questions.e: The combined mean is a weighted average of 20 and 30, and the weights are the numbers of values in each set, which are not given. If the sets are the same size the combined mean is 25; if A has many more values it is closer to 20, and if B has more it is closer to 30. So the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The mean of all the numbers in sets A and B combined

questions.s: The table shows the number of books read last month by each of 20 students.
questions.e: With 20 values, the median is the average of the 10th and 11th values in order. Counting up: 4 students read 1 book (values 1-4) and 6 read 2 books (values 5-10), so the 10th value is 2 and the 11th is 3. The median is (2 + 3)/2 = 2.5. Do not take the middle row of the table or the most common value.
questions.qa: The median number of books read

questions.s: The mean of six numbers is 10. One of the numbers, 16, is removed from the list.
questions.e: The six numbers add up to 6 × 10 = 60. After removing 16, the remaining five add up to 44, so their mean is 44/5 = 8.8, less than 10. Removing a value above the mean always lowers the mean.
questions.qa: The mean of the remaining five numbers

questions.s: x, y and z are positive integers whose mean is 5.
questions.e: The numbers add up to 15, but many sets are possible. For 4, 5, 6 the median is 5, equal to B. For 1, 2, 12 the median is 2, less than 5, and for 1, 7, 7 the median is 7, greater than 5. Knowing the mean does not fix the median.
questions.qa: The median of x, y and z

questions.s: Set S consists of four numbers whose mean is 10.
questions.e: The mean only tells you that the numbers add up to 40. If all four numbers are 10, the range is 0; if they are 5, 5, 15 and 15, the range is exactly 10; and if they are 0, 0, 0 and 40, the range is 40. So the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The range of the numbers in S

questions.s: The list of numbers: 4, 4, 6, n, where n > 6
questions.e: Since n > 6, the list in order is 4, 4, 6, n, so the median is (4 + 6)/2 = 5. The mode is 4, the only value that repeats. So A is greater, whatever the value of n. Without the condition n > 6 (for example n = 4) the comparison could change.

questions.s: The mean of the three numbers 3, 7 and x is 6.
questions.e: The three numbers add up to 3 × 6 = 18, so x = 18 − 3 − 7 = 8, which is less than 9. A quick check: 3 + 7 + 8 = 18, and 18/3 = 6.

questions.s: The mean of the numbers a and b is 10.
questions.e: The information gives a + b = 20 and nothing more. If a = b = 10 the quantities are equal, if a = 15 and b = 5 A is greater, and if a = 5 and b = 15 B is greater. So the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.s:
k is a positive number.
List X: 1, 2, 3
List Y: k, k + 1, k + 2
questions.e: List Y is list X shifted by the same amount, k − 1, for every value. Shifting all values moves the mean by the same amount but leaves every distance from the mean unchanged, so the two standard deviations are equal. The size of k does not matter.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list X
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list Y

questions.s: n is an integer, and the list of numbers is 2, 5, 9, n.
questions.e: The median of four numbers is the average of the middle two, and which numbers are in the middle depends on n. If n = 1, the order is 1, 2, 5, 9 and the median is 3.5. If n = 100, the order is 2, 5, 9, 100 and the median is 7. If n = 5 the median is exactly 5.

questions.s: The average (arithmetic mean) of x, 2x and 3x is 12.
questions.e: x + 2x + 3x = 3 × 12 = 36, so 6x = 36 and x = 6. Then 3x = 18, so the quantities are equal. A common slip is to set 3x equal to the mean, 12; the mean of x, 2x and 3x is 2x, not 3x.

questions.s: Each of seven numbers in a list is an integer from 10 to 20, inclusive, and the median of the seven numbers is 18.
questions.e: The median fixes only the middle value. If the list is 10, 10, 10, 18, 18, 18, 18, the mean is 102/7 ≈ 14.6, less than 18. If it is 18, 18, 18, 18, 20, 20, 20, the mean is 132/7 ≈ 18.9, greater than 18. And 18 seven times gives a mean of exactly 18.
questions.qa: The mean of the seven numbers

questions.s: Five integers have a mean of 10 and a median of 12.
questions.e: The integers add up to 50. With the list 7, 7, 12, 12, 12 (sum 50, median 12) the greatest is 12, less than 15. With 1, 2, 12, 12, 23 the greatest is 23, greater than 15. So the relationship cannot be determined. It is tempting to think the greatest must be well above the mean, but it can be as small as the median.
questions.qa: The greatest of the five integers

questions.s: List X: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. List Y is formed by adding 5 to each number in list X.
questions.e: Adding 5 to every number raises the mean by 5 too, so each number is the same distance from the new mean as before. The spread is unchanged, so the standard deviations are equal. Adding a constant changes the mean, not the standard deviation.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list X
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list Y

questions.s: List X: 1, 4, 7. List Y is formed by multiplying each number in list X by 3.
questions.e: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies every distance from the mean by 3, so the standard deviation of Y is 3 times that of X. Since the values of X are not all equal, its standard deviation is positive, and three times a positive number is larger. Unlike adding a constant, multiplying does change the spread.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list Y
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list X

questions.e: Both lists have the same range, 20, but the means differ: K has mean 15 and L has mean 20. In K the deviations are 5, 5, 5 and 15, and the squared deviations add up to 300; in L they are 10, 0, 0 and 10, adding up to 200. K is more spread out around its mean, so its standard deviation is greater. Equal ranges do not mean equal standard deviations.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list K
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list L

questions.s:
Data: 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 20
The first and third quartiles are the medians of the lower and upper halves of the data.
questions.e: The lower half is 3, 5, 7, 8, with median Q1 = 6, and the upper half is 10, 12, 14, 20, with median Q3 = 13. The interquartile range is 13 − 6 = 7. The range is 20 − 3 = 17, and half of it is 8.5, so B is greater. The single high value 20 widens the range but barely affects the quartiles.
questions.qa: The interquartile range of the data
questions.qb: Half the range of the data

questions.s: In a box plot of a data set, the minimum is 10, the first quartile is 20, the median is 25, the third quartile is 40 and the maximum is 50.
questions.e: Q3 − median = 40 − 25 = 15, and median − minimum = 25 − 10 = 15, so the quantities are equal. Each difference is the length of a different piece of the plot, the right part of the box and the left whisker plus the left part of the box, so read them carefully from the five values given.
questions.qa: The third quartile minus the median

questions.s: Sets X and Y each consist of five numbers. The range of X is greater than the range of Y.
questions.e: A larger range does not guarantee a larger standard deviation. If X is 0, 10, 10, 10, 20 (range 20) and Y is 0, 0, 15, 15, 15 (range 15), Y has the larger standard deviation. If X is 0, 0, 10, 20, 20 and Y is 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, X has the larger one. The range depends only on the two extremes, while the standard deviation depends on every value.

questions.s: The heights of a large group of adults are approximately normally distributed with mean 170 centimeters and standard deviation 8 centimeters.
questions.e: 162 and 178 are one standard deviation below and above the mean. In a normal distribution about 68% of the values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, so the proportion is about 0.68, greater than 0.5. Thinking that one standard deviation on each side covers only 50% is the trap.
questions.qa: The proportion of heights between 162 centimeters and 178 centimeters

questions.s: Scores on a national exam are approximately normally distributed with mean 500 and standard deviation 100. Lin scored 700 on the exam.
questions.e: 700 is two standard deviations above the mean. About 95% of a normal distribution lies within two standard deviations of the mean, leaving about 5% outside, split equally between the two tails. So only about 2.5% of the scores are above 700, less than 5%. Forgetting to split the 5% between the two tails gives the trap answer C.
questions.qa: The percent of scores that are greater than Lin's score

questions.s: The table shows the distribution of the 20 scores on a short quiz.
questions.e: Mean = (10·3 + 20·5 + 30·8 + 40·4)/20 = (30 + 100 + 240 + 160)/20 = 530/20 = 26.5. For the median, the 10th and 11th scores in order are both 30, since 8 scores are 20 or less and 16 are 30 or less. So the median is 30 and B is greater. The mean is pulled down by the scores of 10 and 20.

questions.s: x is an integer, and the list 3, 5, 5, 6, 8, x has exactly one mode.
questions.e: Without x, 5 appears twice and every other number once. If x were 3, 6 or 8, that number would also appear twice and the list would have two modes, which the condition rules out. So x is 5 or a new number, and either way the only mode is 5. It is tempting to answer D because x is unknown, but the condition on the mode settles it.

questions.s: A list of five numbers has a range of 10, and the least number in the list is 3.
questions.e: The greatest number must be 13, but the other three can be anywhere from 3 to 13. For 3, 3, 3, 3, 13 the mean is 5; for 3, 13, 13, 13, 13 it is 11; for 3, 5, 8, 11, 13 it is exactly 8. So the relationship cannot be determined. The midpoint of the extremes, 8, is not the mean unless the values are arranged symmetrically.
questions.qa: The mean of the five numbers

questions.s: The mean of ten numbers is 50. When one of the numbers is replaced by 80, the mean of the ten numbers becomes 52.
questions.e: The sum went from 10 × 50 = 500 to 10 × 52 = 520, an increase of 20. Replacing a number r by 80 increases the sum by 80 − r, so 80 − r = 20 and r = 60, which is greater than 55. The mean rose by only 2, which can make the replaced number seem close to 80 or far below it; work with the sums.

questions.s: Set A consists of five numbers whose median is 10, and set B consists of five numbers whose median is 20.
questions.e: The combined median is the average of the 5th and 6th of the ten numbers, which depends on the values other than the two medians. If A is five 10s and B five 20s, the combined median is 15. If A is 1, 2, 10, 11, 12 and B is 13, 14, 20, 21, 22, it is 12.5. If A is 10, 10, 10, 19, 19 and B is 18, 19, 20, 20, 20, it is 19.
questions.qa: The median of the ten numbers in sets A and B combined

questions.s: List S: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. List T consists of the numbers in S together with one more number, 8.
questions.e: The mean of S is 8, so adding 8 leaves the mean at 8 and adds a value with deviation 0. The total of the squared deviations stays the same but is now spread over more values, so the standard deviation goes down. S has the greater standard deviation. Adding a value equal to the mean always reduces the spread.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list S
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list T

questions.s: In a class, the average score of the boys was 72, the average score of the girls was 84, and the average score of the whole class was 80.
questions.e: With b boys and g girls, 72b + 84g = 80(b + g), so 4g = 8b and g = 2b. The quantities are equal. A shortcut: the class average 80 is 8 above the boys' average and 4 below the girls', so the groups are in the ratio 4 : 8, and there are twice as many girls as boys.
questions.qa: The number of girls in the class
questions.qb: Twice the number of boys in the class

questions.s: Fifty different test scores are listed in order from lowest to highest, and Raj's score is the 40th score in the list.
questions.e: If Raj's score is 40th from the bottom, there are 39 scores before it, so 39 scores are lower. 39 < 40, so B is greater. The off-by-one trap is to count Raj's own score among the lower ones.
questions.qa: The number of scores in the list that are lower than Raj's score

questions.s: Variable X is normally distributed with mean 30 and standard deviation 4. Variable Y is normally distributed with mean 30 and standard deviation 6.
questions.e: 36 is 6 above the mean in both distributions. For X that is 1.5 standard deviations, for Y only 1 standard deviation. The more spread-out distribution, Y, puts more of its values far from the mean, so a larger proportion of Y exceeds 36. B is greater.
questions.qa: The proportion of the values of X that are greater than 36
questions.qb: The proportion of the values of Y that are greater than 36

questions.s: A data set consists of nine numbers. Its box plot shows a minimum of 2, a first quartile of 4, a median of 7, a third quartile of 11 and a maximum of 18. (Here the quartiles are the medians of the four numbers below the median and of the four numbers above it.)
questions.e: Call the numbers in order v1 to v9. Then v1 = 2, v5 = 7, v9 = 18, v2 + v3 = 2 × 4 = 8 and v7 + v8 = 2 × 11 = 22, so the sum is 57 + v4 + v6. Since v3 ≥ 4 (it is the larger of two numbers averaging 4), v4 ≥ 4, and v6 ≥ 7, so the sum is at least 68. A mean of 7 would need a sum of 63, so the mean is always greater than 7. It is tempting to say the unknown values make this undeterminable.
questions.qa: The mean of the nine numbers
questions.qb: The median of the nine numbers

questions.s: Set A consists of the integers from 1 to 20, inclusive. Set B consists of the even integers from 2 to 40, inclusive.
questions.e: Each number in B is exactly twice a number in A: B = {2·1, 2·2, ..., 2·20}. Multiplying every value by 2 doubles every distance from the mean, so it doubles the standard deviation. The quantities are equal. B also has a wider range, but that is fully explained by the doubling.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of set B
questions.qb: Twice the standard deviation of set A

questions.e: Both lists have mean 7.5. S is R with an extra 3 and an extra 12, the two values farthest from the mean (4.5 away). Adding values whose distance from the mean is greater than the typical distance increases the standard deviation, so S is more spread out. Checking: the average squared deviation is 45/4 = 11.25 for R and 85.5/6 = 14.25 for S. Both lists have the same range, which is why the range alone cannot decide this.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list R
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list S

questions.s: x is a number.
questions.e: The effect of adding x depends on where x is. If x = 20, the mean of 10, 20 and 30, the new value has no deviation and the standard deviation decreases, so B is greater. If x = 100, far from the other values, the spread increases and A is greater. So the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of the numbers 10, 20, 30 and x
questions.qb: The standard deviation of the numbers 10, 20 and 30

questions.s: Distribution P is normal with mean 64 and standard deviation 6. Distribution Q is normal with mean 70 and standard deviation 3.
questions.e: For P, 70 is (70 − 64)/6 = 1 standard deviation above the mean, so about 16% of P lies above it. For Q, 76 is (76 − 70)/3 = 2 standard deviations above the mean, so only about 2.5% of Q lies above it. A is greater. Both cut-offs are 6 above their means, which tempts you to answer C; what matters is the distance in standard deviations.
questions.qa: The proportion of the values in P that are greater than 70
questions.qb: The proportion of the values in Q that are greater than 76

questions.s: A variable is normally distributed. Exactly 16% of its values are greater than 58, and exactly 16% of its values are less than 42.
questions.e: A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean, so values that cut off equal tail areas on the two sides are equally far from the mean. 58 and 42 cut off equal tails of 16%, so the mean is halfway between them: (58 + 42)/2 = 50. The standard deviation is not needed (it is about 8, but the comparison does not depend on it).

questions.s: The mean of the numbers in group A is 60, the mean of the numbers in group B is 90, and the mean of all the numbers in the two groups combined is 70.
questions.e: The combined mean 70 is 10 above A's mean and 20 below B's mean. A weighted average sits closer to the group with more members, and the sizes are in the inverse ratio of the distances: A : B = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1. So group A has twice as many numbers as group B. Averaging 60 and 90 gives 75, not 70, which already shows the groups are not the same size.
questions.qa: The number of numbers in group A
questions.qb: The number of numbers in group B

questions.s: The average weight of the 12 boxes in shipment P is greater than the average weight of the 8 boxes in shipment Q.
questions.e: If the averages are p and q, the overall average is (12p + 8q)/20 = 0.6p + 0.4q, while the average of the averages is 0.5p + 0.5q. The difference is 0.1p − 0.1q = 0.1(p − q), which is positive because p > q. The larger shipment has the larger average and so pulls the overall average toward it.
questions.qa: The average weight of all 20 boxes
questions.qb: The average of the two shipment averages

questions.s: The mean of the five numbers 1, 3, 7, 11 and x is equal to their median.
questions.e: The median depends on where x falls, so try each case. If x ≤ 3 the median is 3, and (22 + x)/5 = 3 gives x = −7. If 3 ≤ x ≤ 7 the median is x, and (22 + x)/5 = x gives x = 5.5. If x ≥ 7 the median is 7, and (22 + x)/5 = 7 gives x = 13. Since x could be −7, 5.5 or 13, the relationship cannot be determined. Stopping after finding one solution is the trap.

questions.s: Five different positive integers have a mean of 10.
questions.e: The integers add up to 50. To make the middle one, m, as large as possible, make the two smallest as small as possible (1 and 2) and the two largest as small as possible (m + 1 and m + 2). Then 1 + 2 + m + (m + 1) + (m + 2) = 3m + 6 ≤ 50, so m ≤ 14 2/3, and since m is an integer, m ≤ 14. The list 1, 2, 14, 15, 18 achieves it. So the greatest possible median is 14, less than 15.
questions.qa: The greatest possible value of their median

questions.s: In a list of eight numbers, the greatest number is increased by 10 and the other numbers are unchanged.
questions.e: Increasing one number by 10 increases the sum by 10, so the mean increases by 10/8 = 1.25. The greatest number goes up by 10 while the least stays the same, so the range increases by the full 10. B is greater. The trap is to think both measures move by the same amount.
questions.qa: The increase in the mean of the list
questions.qb: The increase in the range of the list

questions.s: The table shows the frequency distribution of a list of numbers, where k is a nonnegative integer.
questions.e: The median depends on k. If k = 0 there are 19 numbers, and the 10th is 2 (13 numbers are 1 or 2), so the median is 2. If k = 10 there are 29 numbers, and the 15th is 3 (only 13 are 1 or 2), so the median is 3. If k = 7 there are 26 numbers, and the 13th and 14th are 2 and 3, so the median is 2.5. The relationship cannot be determined.

The mean of x, 2x, 3x and 4x is 2.5x, so every number is at most 1.5x away from the mean. A standard deviation is a kind of average distance from the mean, so it cannot exceed the largest distance, 1.5x. Hence it is less than 2x. (Its exact value is about 1.12x.)
questions.qa: The standard deviation of the numbers x, 2x, 3x and 4x

questions.s: The list 1, 2, 2, 3, x has exactly one mode, and the mean of the list is equal to that mode.
questions.e: x cannot be 1 or 3, since either would create a second mode, so the only mode is 2. The mean is then (8 + x)/5 = 2, so x = 2. The list is 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, whose median is 2. The quantities are equal. It looks as if x is unknown, but the two conditions pin it down.

questions.s: List P consists of five numbers that are not all equal, with mean m and standard deviation s. List Q is formed by subtracting m from each number in P and then dividing each result by s.
questions.e: Subtracting m shifts every value and does not change the spread. Dividing every value by s divides every distance from the mean by s, so the new standard deviation is s/s = 1. The quantities are equal. (List Q is the list of z-scores of P, and its mean is 0.) The answer does not depend on the particular numbers in P.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list Q

questions.s: The average (arithmetic mean) of a, b and c is 20, and the average of a and b is 14.
questions.e: a + b + c = 3 × 20 = 60 and a + b = 2 × 14 = 28, so c = 60 − 28 = 32. The quantities are equal. Subtracting the averages, 20 − 14 = 6, and concluding that c is 6 more than 20 (26) is a common error; always convert averages to sums.

questions.s: The mean of a list of ten numbers is 20. Two of the numbers are removed, and the mean of the remaining eight numbers is 18.
questions.e: The removed numbers add up to 10 × 20 − 8 × 18 = 200 − 144 = 56, so they average 28. The greater of them is at least 28: it is 28 if both are 28, which is less than 30, but it is 50 if the other is 6, which is greater than 30. The relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The greater of the two numbers that were removed

questions.s: Lists M and N each consist of five numbers and have the same mean. List M is 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Two of the numbers in list N are 6 and 14.
questions.e: Both lists have mean 10. In M the squared deviations add up to 4 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 4 = 10. In N the numbers 6 and 14 alone contribute 16 + 16 = 32, and the other three numbers can only add more. So N always has the greater standard deviation, whatever its other three numbers are.
questions.qa: The standard deviation of list M
questions.qb: The standard deviation of list N

questions.e: Since x > 100 it is the largest number, so the 50th and 51st numbers in order are 50 and 51 and the median is 50.5. The sum is 4,950 + x, so the mean is (4,950 + x)/100, which is greater than 50.5 exactly when x > 100. The mean of 1 through 99 alone is 50, and one large value pulls the mean above the median.
questions.qa: The mean of the 100 numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 99 and x
questions.qb: The median of the 100 numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 99 and x

questions.s: Five integers have a mean of 6 and a median of 7.
questions.e: The integers add up to 30, with the middle one 7. The two largest are at least 7, so the two smallest add up to at most 30 − 7 − 14 = 9, and the smallest is at most 4. So the range is at least 7 − 4 = 3. It equals 3 for 4, 5, 7, 7, 7, but it can be larger, for example 2, 7, 7, 7, 7 has range 5. The relationship cannot be determined.
questions.qa: The range of the five integers

questions.s: A delivery drone flies 4.5 kilometers in 6 minutes at a constant speed. What is its speed in kilometers per hour?
questions.e: Six minutes is 1/10 of an hour, so in an hour the drone flies 10 × 4.5 = 45 km. The value 0.75 is the speed in kilometers per minute, and 27 multiplies 4.5 by 6 instead of scaling to 60 minutes.

questions.s: A restaurant dishwasher cleans 60 plates in 15 minutes. At this rate, how many minutes does it take to clean 200 plates?
questions.e: The machine cleans 60/15 = 4 plates per minute, so 200 plates take 200/4 = 50 minutes. The choice 800 multiplies 200 by 4 instead of dividing, and 3,000 multiplies 200 by 15.

questions.s: Ali is 3 years older than Bea, and Bea is 5 years older than Cem.
questions.e: Age differences add along the chain: Ali − Cem = (Ali − Bea) + (Bea − Cem) = 3 + 5 = 8, whatever their actual ages. So the quantities are equal. It is tempting to answer that it cannot be determined because no ages are given, but the difference does not depend on them.
questions.qa: Ali's age minus Cem's age, in years

questions.s: Ravi deposits 1,200 dollars in an account that pays 3.5% simple annual interest. How many dollars of interest does he earn in 1 year?
questions.e: Interest for one year is 1,200 × 0.035 = 42 dollars. A common slip is to use 0.35 instead of 0.035, which gives 420 dollars; 3.5% is 3.5 hundredths.

questions.s: Each bottle holds 750 milliliters of juice. How many full bottles are needed to fill a 12-liter punch bowl exactly?
questions.e: Twelve liters is 12,000 milliliters, and 12,000/750 = 16 bottles. Dividing 12 by 750 without converting liters to milliliters leads to the decimal slips 1.6 or 160.

questions.s: A fruit seller in Manila buys 50 mangoes for a total of 20 dollars and sells all of them for 0.60 dollar each. What is her profit?
questions.e: Her revenue is 50 × 0.60 = 30 dollars and her cost is 20 dollars, so the profit is 10 dollars. Choosing 30 dollars gives the revenue rather than the profit, and 20 dollars is the cost.

questions.s: A juice drink is made from 1 part concentrate and 4 parts water by volume. Which of the following mixtures have the same concentration as this drink? Indicate all such mixtures.
questions.e: The drink has concentrate and water in the ratio 1 : 4, so concentrate is 1/5 of the total. 2 : 8 and 0.5 : 2 both reduce to 1 : 4, and 1 liter in 5 liters total means 4 liters of water. 3 : 15 is 1 : 5, which is weaker, and 4 : 1 reverses the ratio.
o: 2 liters of concentrate with 8 liters of water
3 liters of concentrate with 15 liters of water
0.5 liter of concentrate with 2 liters of water
1 liter of concentrate in 5 liters of drink in total
4 liters of concentrate with 1 liter of water

questions.s: A ferry leaves the harbor every 25 minutes, with the first departure at 6:10 a.m. and the last at 9:30 a.m. How many ferries leave during this period, including the first and the last?
questions.e: From 6:10 to 9:30 is 200 minutes, which is 200/25 = 8 intervals of 25 minutes. Eight intervals have 9 endpoints, so 9 ferries leave. Answering 8 counts the gaps instead of the departures, the classic fence-post error.

questions.s: Solution X is 30 liters of a 20% acid solution, and solution Y is 20 liters of a 30% acid solution. All of X and all of Y are mixed together.
questions.e: The mixture contains 0.20 × 30 + 0.30 × 20 = 6 + 6 = 12 liters of acid in 50 liters, which is 24%. Quantity B is greater. Averaging 20% and 30% to get 25% ignores that there is more of the weaker solution.
questions.qa: The percent of acid in the mixture

questions.s: An investment that earns a fixed rate of interest compounded annually doubles in value every 8 years. How many years does it take for the original investment to become 8 times as large?
questions.e: Becoming 8 times as large means doubling three times (2 × 2 × 2 = 8), and each doubling takes 8 years, so it takes 3 × 8 = 24 years. The choice 16 allows only two doublings, which makes the money 4 times as large, not 8; growth by a multiple is counted in doublings, not added up.

questions.s: A shop lowers the price of a blender by 20%. By what percent must the new price be increased to bring it back to the original price?
questions.e: If the original price is 100, the reduced price is 80, and getting back to 100 needs an increase of 20, which is 20/80 = 25% of the new price. Answering 20% forgets that the increase is measured from the lower price.

questions.s: In 2018, Mei's age was 1/4 of her father's age. In 2026, Mei's age is 2/5 of her father's age. How old is Mei's father in 2026?
questions.e: If the father was f in 2018, Mei was f/4, and eight years later f/4 + 8 = (2/5)(f + 8). Multiplying by 20: 5f + 160 = 8f + 64, so f = 32. In 2026 he is 40 and Mei is 16, and 16/40 = 2/5. Answering 32 gives his age in 2018.

questions.s: Printer A prints a batch of brochures in 40 minutes. Printers A and B working together print the same batch in 24 minutes. How many minutes would printer B alone take?
questions.e: Together they print 1/24 of the batch per minute and A prints 1/40, so B prints 1/24 − 1/40 = 5/120 − 3/120 = 1/60 of the batch per minute and needs 60 minutes. Subtracting the times (40 − 24 = 16) is wrong because rates, not times, add.

questions.s: Kim walked for x hours at 5 kilometers per hour and then ran for y hours at 10 kilometers per hour, covering 20 kilometers in all. Both x and y are positive.
questions.e: The condition is 5x + 10y = 20, so x = 4 − 2y. If y = 1, then x = 2 and Quantity A is greater; if y = 1.5, then x = 1 and Quantity B is greater (and at y = 4/3 they are equal). The relationship cannot be determined. Assuming she must have run less time because running is faster is the trap.

questions.s: A car travels at a constant 25 meters per second. How many kilometers does it travel in 12 minutes?
questions.e: Twelve minutes is 720 seconds, so the car covers 25 × 720 = 18,000 meters, which is 18 kilometers. The choice 90 is the speed in kilometers per hour, and 300 multiplies 25 by 12 without converting minutes to seconds.

questions.s: Which of the following investments earn more than 300 dollars in interest? Indicate all such investments.
questions.e: Both simple-interest options earn exactly 300 dollars (2,000 × 0.05 × 3 and 1,500 × 0.10 × 2), which is not more than 300. Compounding adds interest on interest: 2,000 × 1.05³ − 2,000 = 315.25, 1,500 × 1.1² − 1,500 = 315 and 3,000 × 1.02⁵ − 3,000 ≈ 312.24. So the three compound investments qualify.
o: 2,000 dollars at 5% simple interest for 3 years
2,000 dollars at 5% compounded annually for 3 years
1,500 dollars at 10% simple interest for 2 years
1,500 dollars at 10% compounded annually for 2 years
3,000 dollars at 2% compounded annually for 5 years

questions.s: A 12-liter batch of paint is made from 3 liters of blue paint and 9 liters of white paint. How many liters of blue paint must be added so that blue paint makes up 40% of the batch?
questions.e: After adding x liters, (3 + x)/(12 + x) = 0.4, so 3 + x = 4.8 + 0.4x, 0.6x = 1.8 and x = 3. Check: 6 liters of blue in 15 liters is 40%. Taking 40% of 12 (4.8) forgets that the batch grows as blue is added, and 1.8 is 0.6x rather than x.

questions.s: Kofi is 24 years old. He is twice as old as Esi was when Kofi was as old as Esi is now. How old is Esi now?
questions.e: Kofi is older; call the gap 24 − E. Kofi was E years old 24 − E years ago, when Esi was E − (24 − E) = 2E − 24. Then 24 = 2(2E − 24), so 2E − 24 = 12 and E = 18. Check: 6 years ago Kofi was 18 and Esi 12, and 24 = 2 × 12. The answer 12 is Esi's age at that earlier time.

questions.s: Equal positive amounts P are invested for 10 years: account A at 7% simple annual interest and account B at 5% interest compounded annually.
questions.e: Account A earns 10 × 0.07P = 0.70P. Account B earns (1.05¹⁰ − 1)P ≈ (1.629 − 1)P = 0.629P. Since P is positive, A earns more. Compounding does not beat simple interest here, because 10 years is not long enough to make up a 2-point gap in the rate.
questions.qa: The interest earned by account A
questions.qb: The interest earned by account B

questions.s: Two cyclists start 60 kilometers apart and ride toward each other along a straight road at 18 and 12 kilometers per hour. At the same moment, a bird starts from the first cyclist and flies back and forth between the two cyclists at 40 kilometers per hour until they meet. How many kilometers does the bird fly?
questions.e: There is no need to add up the separate trips. The cyclists close the gap at 18 + 12 = 30 km/h, so they meet after 60/30 = 2 hours. The bird flies the whole time at 40 km/h and covers 40 × 2 = 80 km.

questions.s: Four identical machines can complete a job in 6 hours. A manager starts the job with n of these machines and adds 2 more machines after 3 hours. The job must take at least 5 hours and at most 6 hours from the start. Which of the following could be n? Indicate all such values.
questions.e: The job is 4 × 6 = 24 machine-hours. In the first 3 hours n machines do 3n, and then n + 2 machines finish the rest in (24 − 3n)/(n + 2) hours. For n = 3 the total time is 3 + 15/5 = 6 hours, and for n = 4 it is 3 + 12/6 = 5 hours. With n = 2 it takes 7.5 hours, and with n = 5 only about 4.3 hours.

questions.s: During a sale, a store takes 10% off the price of a sofa, then 20% off the reduced price, and finally 25% off that price at the register. The final price is the same as a single discount of what percent off the original price?
questions.e: The final price is 0.90 × 0.80 × 0.75 = 0.54 of the original, which is a single discount of 46%. Adding the discounts gives 55%, too much because each later discount applies to a smaller price. The value 54% is the fraction of the price that remains, not the discount.

questions.s: A company's revenue rose 10% in its first year, fell 10% in its second year and rose 10% in its third year. What was the total percent change in revenue over the three years?
questions.e: Multiply the yearly factors: 1.1 × 0.9 × 1.1 = 1.089, an increase of 8.9%. Adding the percents (+10 − 10 + 10) gives 10%, which ignores that a 10% fall from a larger amount removes more than a 10% rise added. 33.1% leaves out the fall entirely.

questions.s: A landscaper needs to spread mulch 8 centimeters deep over a garden bed with an area of 45 square meters. Mulch is sold in 60-liter bags. How many bags are needed? (1 cubic meter = 1,000 liters)
questions.e: Eight centimeters is 0.08 meter, so the mulch volume is 45 × 0.08 = 3.6 cubic meters, or 3,600 liters, which fills 3,600/60 = 60 bags. Writing 8 cm as 0.008 m gives 6 bags, ten times too few; 7.5 divides the area by 6 and ignores the depth.

questions.s: A local train leaves a station at 9:00 a.m. and travels at 60 kilometers per hour. An express train leaves the same station at 10:00 a.m. on a parallel track in the same direction and travels at 90 kilometers per hour. At what time does the express train catch up with the local train?
questions.e: By 10:00 a.m. the local train is 60 km ahead. The express gains 90 − 60 = 30 km each hour, so it closes the gap in 60/30 = 2 hours, at 12:00 noon. Counting the 2 hours from 9:00 instead of from 10:00, or dividing 60 by 90, gives other times.

questions.s: A cyclist in Amsterdam rides at a constant speed of 18 kilometers per hour. How many minutes does it take her to ride 12 kilometers?
questions.e: Time = distance ÷ speed = 12/18 hour = 2/3 hour. Converting to minutes, 2/3 × 60 = 40 minutes. Choosing 90 comes from dividing the wrong way (18 ÷ 12 = 1.5 hours).

questions.s: An office printer prints 45 pages per minute. At this rate, how many pages can it print in 3 hours 20 minutes?
questions.e: 3 hours 20 minutes is 3 × 60 + 20 = 200 minutes, so the printer makes 45 × 200 = 9,000 pages. Reading 3 hours 20 minutes as 3.2 hours (192 minutes) gives 8,640, and ignoring the 20 minutes gives 8,100.

questions.s: A 40-liter tank holds a solution that is 15% salt by volume. If 10 liters of pure water are added, what percent of the new solution is salt?
questions.e: The tank contains 0.15 × 40 = 6 liters of salt, and adding water does not change that amount. The new volume is 50 liters, so salt is 6/50 = 12% of it. Subtracting 10 from 15 to get 5% treats liters of water as percentage points.

questions.s: Lena deposits 2,500 dollars in an account that pays 4% simple annual interest. How much interest does the account earn in 3 years?
questions.e: Simple interest is principal × rate × time = 2,500 × 0.04 × 3 = 300 dollars. The value 312.16 dollars is the compound-interest amount, which this account does not pay, and 2,800 dollars is the balance rather than the interest.

questions.s: A shop in Nairobi buys a desk lamp for 40 dollars and sells it for 52 dollars. The profit is what percent of the cost?
questions.e: The profit is 52 − 40 = 12, dollars and as a percent of the cost of 40 dollars it is 12/40 = 30%. Dividing by the selling price (12/52, about 23%) uses the wrong base, and 130% is the selling price as a percent of cost.

questions.s: Kwame is now 4 times as old as his daughter Ama. In 5 years, the sum of their ages will be 50. How old is Ama now?
questions.e: If Ama is x, Kwame is 4x, and in 5 years their ages add to (x + 5) + (4x + 5) = 5x + 10 = 50, so x = 8. Writing 5x = 50 forgets that both people age 5 years and gives 10; 32 is Kwame's age.

questions.s: Mateo saves 15 dollars in the first week and each week saves 5 dollars more than the week before. How much does he save in the 12th week?
questions.e: Week 12 comes 11 increases after week 1, so the amount is 15 + 11 × 5 = 70 dollars. Using 12 increases gives 75, dollars and 510 dollars is the total saved over all 12 weeks, not the 12th week's amount.

questions.s: A high-speed train travels at 72 kilometers per hour. What is this speed in meters per second?
questions.e: 72 kilometers is 72,000 meters and 1 hour is 3,600 seconds, so the speed is 72,000/3,600 = 20 meters per second. The value 1,200 is meters per minute, and 259.2 comes from multiplying by 3.6 instead of dividing.

questions.s: A tap fills an empty 450-liter water tank at a constant rate of 18 liters per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill the tank?
questions.e: Time = amount ÷ rate = 450 ÷ 18 = 25 minutes. A quick check: 18 × 25 = 450 liters. Multiplying 450 by 18 would give liters × liters per minute, which is not a time.

questions.s: Each painter on a hotel crew paints 3 rooms per day. The hotel needs at least 40 rooms painted in 2 days. Which of the following numbers of painters would be enough? Indicate all such numbers.
questions.e: In 2 days one painter paints 3 × 2 = 6 rooms, so n painters paint 6n rooms and we need 6n ≥ 40, that is n ≥ 6⅔. The smallest whole crew is 7, so 7, 8 and 10 all work. Six painters manage only 36 rooms, which falls short.

questions.s: Chen invests 1,000 dollars at 10% interest compounded annually. What is the value of the investment at the end of 2 years?
questions.e: Each year the value is multiplied by 1.10: 1,000 → 1,100 → 1,210. Simple interest would give 1,200, dollars and 1,331 dollars is the value after 3 years, not 2.

questions.s: A café blends 3 kilograms of coffee costing 12 dollars per kilogram with 2 kilograms of coffee costing 17 dollars per kilogram. What is the cost per kilogram of the blend?
questions.e: The blend costs 3 × 12 + 2 × 17 = 36 + 34 = 70 dollars for 5 kilograms, or 70/5 = 14 dollars per kilogram. The plain average of the two prices, 14.50 dollars, ignores that there is more of the cheaper coffee; 15 dollars swaps the weights.

questions.s: A food vendor in Lima sells 120 empanadas at 2.50 dollars each. Her ingredients cost 165 dollars in total, and she pays 45 dollars to rent the stall. What is her profit, in dollars?
questions.e: Revenue is 120 × 2.50 = 300, dollars and total costs are 165 + 45 = 210, dollars so profit is 300 − 210 = 90 dollars. Forgetting the stall rent would give 135 dollars.

questions.s: Sofia is 7 years older than her brother Mateo. Six years ago, Sofia was twice as old as Mateo was then. How old is Mateo now?
questions.e: Six years ago Mateo was M − 6 and Sofia was M + 1, so M + 1 = 2(M − 6), giving M = 13. Check: 6 years ago they were 7 and 14. Answering 7 gives Mateo's age at that earlier time, and 20 is Sofia's age now.

questions.s: A car uses 6.5 liters of fuel per 100 kilometers. How many liters of fuel does it use on a 340-kilometer trip?
questions.e: The trip is 340/100 = 3.4 hundred kilometers, so the car uses 6.5 × 3.4 = 22.1 liters. Dividing 340 by 6.5 (about 52.3) would give kilometers per liter only if 6.5 were liters per kilometer, which it is not.

questions.s: A theater has 22 seats in the first row, and each row after that has 2 more seats than the row in front of it. How many seats are in the first 10 rows altogether?
questions.e: Row 10 has 22 + 9 × 2 = 40 seats. The total is the number of rows times the average of the first and last rows: 10 × (22 + 40)/2 = 310. Using 22 + 10 × 2 = 42 for the last row is the usual off-by-one slip.

questions.s: Olga drives 240 kilometers at a constant speed that is at least 60 and at most 80 kilometers per hour. Which of the following could be the number of hours the drive takes? Indicate all such numbers.
questions.e: At 80 km/h the drive takes 240/80 = 3 hours, and at 60 km/h it takes 240/60 = 4 hours, so the time is anywhere from 3 to 4 hours. That allows 3, 3.5 and 4. A time of 2.5 hours would need 96 km/h, and 4.5 hours would mean only about 53 km/h.

questions.s: A pack of 6 bottles of water costs 4.20 dollars. Which of the following purchases cost less per bottle than the 6-pack? Indicate all such purchases.
questions.e: The 6-pack costs 4.20/6 = 0.70 dollars per bottle. Per bottle, the others cost 0.65 (pack of 4), 0.675 (pack of 12), 0.69 (pack of 10), 0.71 (pack of 24) and 0.75 (single). So the packs of 4, 12 and 10 are cheaper; the 24-pack looks like a bulk bargain but costs slightly more per bottle.

questions.s: Pipe A alone can fill a pool in 6 hours, and pipe B alone can fill it in 3 hours. How many hours does it take to fill the empty pool with both pipes open?
questions.e: Pipe A fills 1/6 of the pool per hour and pipe B fills 1/3, so together they fill 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 per hour and need 2 hours. Averaging the times (4.5 hours) is the classic trap: working together must be faster than the faster pipe alone.

questions.s: A short video had 500 views on its first day online. On each following day it had 3 times as many views as on the day before. How many views did it have on the 5th day?
questions.e: Day 5 is 4 tripling steps after day 1, so the views are 500 × 3⁴ = 500 × 81 = 40,500. Multiplying 500 by 3 × 5 = 15 gives 7,500, which treats repeated tripling as one multiplication; 13,500 uses only 3 steps.

questions.s: Chen drives from Shenzhen to a nearby city at an average speed of 60 kilometers per hour and returns along the same road at 40 kilometers per hour. What is his average speed, in kilometers per hour, for the whole round trip?
questions.e: Pick a one-way distance of 120 km: the trip out takes 2 hours and the return 3 hours, so 240 km in 5 hours is 48 km/h. The answer does not depend on the distance chosen. Averaging 60 and 40 to get 50 ignores that he spends more time at the slower speed.

questions.s: At 9:00 a.m., one train leaves Lyon for Geneva and another leaves Geneva for Lyon on a parallel track. The cities are 300 kilometers apart by rail, and the trains travel at constant speeds of 70 and 80 kilometers per hour. At what time do the trains pass each other?
questions.e: Moving toward each other, the trains close the gap at 70 + 80 = 150 km/h, so they meet after 300/150 = 2 hours, at 11:00 a.m. Using one train's speed (300/80 = 3.75 hours → 12:45 p.m.) ignores that the other train is also covering distance.

questions.s: Amara starts jogging along a riverside path at 8 kilometers per hour. Fifteen minutes later, Priya starts from the same point along the same path at 10 kilometers per hour. How many minutes after Priya starts does she catch up with Amara?
questions.e: In 15 minutes Amara gets 8 × 1/4 = 2 km ahead. Priya gains 10 − 8 = 2 km each hour, so she needs 1 hour = 60 minutes. The choice 75 counts from Amara's start, not Priya's.

questions.s: An escalator in a metro station is 30 meters long and its steps move upward at 0.5 meter per second. Olga walks up the moving escalator at 1 meter per second relative to the steps. How many seconds does it take her to get from the bottom to the top?
questions.e: Her speed relative to the ground is her walking speed plus the escalator's: 1 + 0.5 = 1.5 m/s. The time is 30/1.5 = 20 seconds. Using only her walking speed gives 30 seconds, and subtracting the speeds gives 60.

questions.s: A plane flies 1,800 kilometers with a steady tailwind in 3 hours and returns the same 1,800 kilometers against the same wind in 4 hours. What is the plane's speed in still air, in kilometers per hour?
questions.e: With the wind the ground speed is 1,800/3 = 600 km/h, and against it 1,800/4 = 450 km/h. Still-air speed p and wind w satisfy p + w = 600 and p − w = 450, so p = 525 (and w = 75). The value 514 is the average speed of the round trip (3,600 km in 7 hours), which is not the still-air speed.

questions.s: A bus travels the first 120 kilometers of a route at 60 kilometers per hour and the remaining 90 kilometers at a constant speed v kilometers per hour. If its average speed for the whole route is at least 63 kilometers per hour, which of the following could be v? Indicate all such values.
questions.e: An average of at least 63 km/h over 210 km means a total time of at most 210/63 = 10/3 hours. The first part takes 120/60 = 2 hours, leaving at most 4/3 hours for 90 km, so v ≥ 90 ÷ 4/3 = 67.5. Thus 67.5, 70, 75 and 90 work; 65 is tempting because it exceeds 63, but the slow first part must be made up.

questions.s: A dripping faucet releases 1 drop of water every 2 seconds, and 20 drops make 1 milliliter. How many liters of water does the faucet waste in one week?
questions.e: A week has 7 × 24 × 3,600 = 604,800 seconds, so there are 302,400 drops, which is 302,400/20 = 15,120 mL = 15.12 liters. Forgetting that a drop falls only every 2 seconds doubles the answer to 30.24, and a slip in the mL-to-L step gives 1.512 or 151.2.

questions.s: The wheels of a delivery bicycle have a circumference of 1.8 meters. If each wheel turns 500 times per minute, what is the bicycle's speed in kilometers per hour?
questions.e: Each turn moves the bicycle 1.8 m, so it covers 1.8 × 500 = 900 m per minute. In an hour that is 54,000 m = 54 km, so the speed is 54 km/h. The choice 15 is the speed in meters per second, and 900 is meters per minute.

questions.s: Machine A makes 300 bolts in 5 hours. Machines A and B working together make 300 bolts in 3 hours. How many hours would machine B alone take to make 300 bolts?
questions.e: A makes 300/5 = 60 bolts per hour and together they make 300/3 = 100 per hour, so B makes 40 per hour and needs 300/40 = 7.5 hours. Subtracting the times (5 − 3 = 2) is wrong because rates add, not times.

questions.s: Six workers can build a garden wall in 10 days. They work for 4 days, and then 3 more workers who work at the same rate join them. How many days in total does it take to build the wall?
questions.e: The wall takes 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. After 4 days, 24 worker-days are done and 36 remain; 9 workers finish them in 36/9 = 4 days, for a total of 8 days. The choice 4 is only the second stage, and 6 2/3 is the time for 9 workers to build the whole wall.

questions.s: An inlet pipe can fill an empty rainwater tank in 4 hours, and a drain can empty the full tank in 6 hours. If the tank is empty and both the inlet and the drain are open, how many hours does it take to fill the tank?
questions.e: Each hour the inlet adds 1/4 of the tank and the drain removes 1/6, a net gain of 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 of the tank. Filling the whole tank therefore takes 12 hours. Adding the rates (1/4 + 1/6) treats the drain as a second inlet and gives the wrong 2.4 hours.

questions.s: Ivan can paint a fence alone in 6 hours, and Malik can paint the same fence alone in 4 hours. Ivan works alone for 1 hour, and then Malik joins him until the fence is finished. How many hours after Ivan starts is the fence finished?
questions.e: In the first hour Ivan paints 1/6 of the fence, leaving 5/6. Together they paint 1/6 + 1/4 = 5/12 per hour, so the rest takes (5/6) ÷ (5/12) = 2 hours, for 3 hours in all. The choice 3.4 adds 1 hour to the 2.4 hours they would need for the whole fence, forgetting that Ivan already did part of it.

questions.s: A print shop has three presses. Press A prints 1,200 sheets per hour, press B prints 900 sheets per hour, and press C prints 600 sheets per hour. An order of 4,500 sheets must be printed in at most 3 hours. Which of the following could complete the order on time? Indicate all such choices.
questions.e: The order needs a combined rate of at least 4,500/3 = 1,500 sheets per hour. A and C give 1,800, B and C give exactly 1,500 and A and B give 2,100, so all three pairs work. Press A alone reaches only 3,600 sheets in 3 hours, and B alone only 2,700.

questions.s: In a warehouse in Rotterdam, 8 people working at the same rate pack 960 boxes in 6 hours. At this rate, how many people are needed to pack 1,200 boxes in 5 hours?
questions.e: One person packs 960/(8 × 6) = 20 boxes per hour. To pack 1,200 boxes in 5 hours the team must pack 240 boxes per hour, which takes 240/20 = 12 people. Scaling only by the number of boxes (8 × 1,200/960 = 10) forgets that there is less time.

questions.s: Machine Y works twice as fast as machine X. Working together, the two machines complete a job in 4 hours. How many hours would machine X take to complete the job alone?
questions.e: If X takes x hours, its rate is 1/x and Y's rate is 2/x, so 3/x = 1/4 and x = 12. Machine Y alone would take 6 hours, which is the most common wrong pick. Check: 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/4.

questions.s: Three sorting robots in a parcel center sort 150, 200 and 250 parcels per hour. The first two start together, and the third robot starts 1 hour later. How many hours after the first two start will the three robots have sorted a total of 2,750 parcels?
questions.e: Let t be the hours since the start. The total is 150t + 200t + 250(t − 1) = 600t − 250, and setting this equal to 2,750 gives 600t = 3,000, so t = 5. Ignoring the late start gives 2,750/600, about 4.6 hours.

questions.s: A 30-liter batch of fruit drink is 20% juice. How many liters of water must be added so that the drink is 12% juice?
questions.e: The batch contains 0.20 × 30 = 6 liters of juice. For 6 liters to be 12% of the drink, the total must be 6/0.12 = 50 liters, so 50 − 30 = 20 liters of water must be added. Choosing 50 gives the new total, not the amount added.

questions.s: A foundry melts 10 kilograms of an alloy that is 30% copper together with 15 kilograms of a second alloy. The result is 42% copper. What percent of the second alloy is copper?
questions.e: Copper balance: 0.30 × 10 + (x/100) × 15 = 0.42 × 25 = 10.5, so 15x/100 = 7.5 and x = 50. Swapping the two weights (putting 15 kg with 30%) leads to 60%. Check: 3 + 7.5 = 10.5 kg of copper in 25 kg.

questions.s: A chemist mixes 40 milliliters of a 25% acid solution with v milliliters of a 60% acid solution, where 20 ≤ v ≤ 60. Which of the following could be the acid concentration of the mixture? Indicate all such concentrations.
questions.e: The concentration rises as more 60% solution is added. With v = 20 it is (10 + 12)/60 ≈ 36.7%, and with v = 60 it is (10 + 36)/100 = 46%, so every value from about 36.7% to 46% is possible: 37.5%, 40% and 45%. 35% is too low (it would need less than 20 mL of the strong solution) and 50% is too high.

questions.s: A 20-kilogram sack of mixed nuts contains almonds and cashews in the ratio 3 : 2 by weight. How many kilograms of cashews must be added to make the ratio 1 : 1?
questions.e: The sack holds 3/5 × 20 = 12 kg of almonds and 8 kg of cashews. Equal amounts require 12 kg of cashews, so 4 kg must be added. Choosing 8 or 12 confuses the amount already present with the amount to add.

questions.s: A 50-liter tank of fuel blend is 10% ethanol. How many liters of the blend must be drained and replaced with pure ethanol so that the tank, again holding 50 liters, is 28% ethanol?
questions.e: The tank starts with 5 liters of ethanol. Draining y liters removes 0.1y of ethanol and adding y liters of pure ethanol adds y, so 5 + 0.9y = 0.28 × 50 = 14 and y = 10. Simply adding 9 liters (14 − 5) forgets that some ethanol leaves with the drained blend.

questions.s: A tea merchant in Colombo blends tea costing 8 dollars per kilogram with tea costing 14 dollars per kilogram to make 30 kilograms of a blend worth 10 dollars per kilogram. How many kilograms of the 8-dollar tea are used?
questions.e: If a kilograms of the cheaper tea are used, 8a + 14(30 − a) = 10 × 30 = 300, so 420 − 6a = 300 and a = 20. The choice 10 is the amount of the 14-dollar tea. Since 10 dollars is closer to 8 than to 14, more of the cheaper tea is needed, which rules out 15 or less.

questions.s: A 20-liter container is full of milk. Four liters are removed and replaced with water, and the mixture is stirred. Then 4 liters of the mixture are removed and replaced with water again. How many liters of milk are now in the container?
questions.e: Each replacement removes 4/20 = 20% of whatever milk is present. After the first, 16 liters of milk remain; the second removes 20% of 16 = 3.2 liters, leaving 12.8. The answer 12 assumes 4 liters of pure milk leave both times, but the second 4 liters is only 80% milk.

questions.s: A nurse needs 600 milliliters of a 5% saline solution and has only 9% and 3% solutions. How many milliliters of the 9% solution should she use?
questions.e: With s mL of 9% solution, 0.09s + 0.03(600 − s) = 0.05 × 600 = 30, so 0.06s = 12 and s = 200. The answer 400 is the amount of 3% solution. Since 5% is closer to 3% than to 9%, most of the mixture must be the weaker solution.

questions.s: Amara invests 8,000 dollars at 5% interest compounded annually. What is the value of the investment at the end of 3 years?
questions.e: The value is 8,000 × 1.05³ = 8,000 × 1.157625 = 9,261 dollars. Simple interest would give 8,000 + 3 × 400 = 9,200 dollars, which is less because it never earns interest on interest; 1,261 dollars is only the interest earned.

questions.s: A small business in Accra borrows 12,000 dollars at simple annual interest and repays a total of 14,880 dollars at the end of 4 years. What is the annual interest rate, in percent?
questions.e: The interest paid is 14,880 − 12,000 = 2,880 dollars over 4 years, or 720 dollars per year. As a share of the principal, 720/12,000 = 0.06, so the rate is 6%. Dividing by the repaid total (14,880) instead of the amount borrowed gives about 4.8%, a wrong-base error.

questions.s: Sofia deposits 5,000 dollars in a savings account that pays 8% annual interest compounded semiannually (every six months). What is the balance at the end of 1 year?
questions.e: Semiannual compounding at 8% per year means 4% is added every six months, twice in the year: 5,000 × 1.04² = 5,408 dollars. Annual compounding would give 5,400, and 5,832 comes from applying the full 8% in each six-month period. 5,412.16 would be quarterly compounding.

questions.s: Kwame invests a total of 10,000 dollars, part at 3% and the rest at 7% simple annual interest. After one year he has earned 540 dollars in interest. How much did he invest at 7%?
questions.e: If x dollars earn 3%, then 0.03x + 0.07(10,000 − x) = 540, so 700 − 0.04x = 540 and x = 4,000. The amount at 7% is 10,000 − 4,000 = 6,000 dollars. The trap is to stop at x = 4,000, which is the amount at 3%.

questions.s: Which of the following annual interest rates, compounded annually, would make an investment of 1,000 dollars grow to more than 1,200 dollars in 2 years? Indicate all such rates.
questions.e: The rate r must satisfy (1 + r)² > 1.2. At 9.5%, 1.095² = 1.199025, giving 1,199.03 dollars, just short; at 10%, 1.1² = 1.21 gives 1,210 dollars. So only 10% and 12% work. Halving the 20% growth to get 10% is close, but 9% and 9.5% are below the cutoff of about 9.54%.

questions.s: Priya deposits 5,000 dollars for 2 years at 10% annual interest. How much more interest does she earn if the interest is compounded annually than if it is simple interest?
questions.e: Simple interest is 5,000 × 0.10 × 2 = 1,000 dollars. Compounded, the balance is 5,000 × 1.1² = 6,050, so the interest is 1,050 dollars. The difference, 50 dollars, is the interest earned in year 2 on year 1's 500 dollars of interest. 1,050 is the compound interest itself, not the difference.

questions.s: Mateo buys a laptop for 3,600 dollars with a loan that charges 5% simple annual interest for 2 years. He repays the loan and all the interest in 24 equal monthly payments. How much is each payment?
questions.e: The interest is 3,600 × 0.05 × 2 = 360 dollars, so he repays 3,960 dollars in total, and 3,960/24 = 165 dollars per month. Including only one year of interest gives 157.50, and ignoring interest gives 150. Splitting into 12 payments instead of 24 gives 330.

questions.s: Chen made a single deposit into an account that pays 5% interest compounded annually. Two years later, with no other deposits or withdrawals, the balance was 6,615 dollars. What was the amount of the deposit?
questions.e: Two years of 5% growth multiply the deposit by 1.05² = 1.1025, so the deposit was 6,615/1.1025 = 6,000 dollars. Dividing by 1.10 (simple interest, giving 6,013.64) or by 1.05 once (6,300) undoes the growth incorrectly. Subtracting 10% of 6,615 gives 5,953.50, which uses the wrong base.

questions.s: A boutique marks up the price of a scarf 40% above its cost and later sells it at a 25% discount off the marked price. The profit is what percent of the cost?
questions.e: If the cost is 100, the marked price is 140 and the sale price is 75% of 140 = 105, a profit of 5%. Subtracting 25 from 40 to get 15% is the trap: the discount is taken from the larger marked price, so it removes 35, not 25.

questions.s: A street vendor in Bangkok sold a used bicycle for 63 dollars, which was a loss of 10% of what he had paid for it. How much had he paid for the bicycle?
questions.e: A 10% loss means the selling price is 90% of the cost: 0.9c = 63, so c = 70 dollars. Adding 10% of 63 to get 69.30 uses the selling price as the base, but the loss is a percent of the cost.

questions.s: A coffee cooperative in Kenya sells 800 kilograms of coffee at 9.50 dollars per kilogram. Its costs are 1,800 dollars in fixed costs plus 5.25 dollars per kilogram produced. What is its profit, in dollars?
questions.e: Revenue is 800 × 9.50 = 7,600 dollars. Costs are 1,800 + 800 × 5.25 = 1,800 + 4,200 = 6,000 dollars, so the profit is 1,600 dollars. Forgetting the fixed costs gives 3,400 dollars.

questions.s: A start-up in Lagos makes solar lamps. Its fixed costs are 4,200 dollars per month, each lamp costs 18 dollars to make, and each lamp sells for 32 dollars. What is the least number of lamps it must make and sell in a month to make a profit?
questions.e: Each lamp contributes 32 − 18 = 14 dollars toward the fixed costs, and 4,200/14 = 300 lamps exactly cover them with zero profit. A profit needs at least one more lamp: 301. The choice 300 is the break-even point, and 132 divides 4,200 by the price, ignoring the cost of each lamp.

questions.s: A store in Toronto reduces the price of a 250-dollar jacket by 20%, and later reduces the new price by a further 15%. What is the final price?
questions.e: After the first cut the price is 0.8 × 250 = 200 dollars, and 15% off that leaves 0.85 × 200 = 170 dollars. Adding the discounts to 35% and taking 35% off 250 gives 162.50, which is wrong because the second discount applies to the already reduced price.

questions.s: A retailer buys jackets for 60 dollars each. She will sell them at a 10% discount off the marked price and wants a profit of at least 20% of the cost. Which of the following marked prices would meet her goal? Indicate all such prices.
questions.e: The selling price must be at least 1.2 × 60 = 72 dollars, and the selling price is 0.9 of the marked price, so the marked price must be at least 72/0.9 = 80 dollars. That allows 80, 84 and 90. Marking at 72 is the trap: after the discount it sells for only 64.80.

questions.s: Two partners invest 30,000 dollars and 50,000 dollars in a bakery and share its profit in proportion to their investments. If the second partner receives 3,000 dollars more than the first, what is the total profit?
questions.e: The shares are in the ratio 30 : 50 = 3 : 5, so the profit splits into 8 equal parts and the difference is 2 parts. If 2 parts are 3,000 dollars, 1 part is 1,500 and the total is 8 × 1,500 = 12,000 dollars. The choice 7,500 is the second partner's share alone.

questions.s: A bookseller's profit on each book is 20% of the book's selling price. The profit is what percent of the cost of the book?
questions.e: Take a selling price of 100: the profit is 20, so the cost is 80, and 20/80 = 25% of cost. Answering 20% ignores the change of base. The value 125% is the selling price as a percent of the cost.

questions.s: The ratio of Yuki's age to her mother's age is now 2 : 7. In 10 years the ratio will be 4 : 9. How old is Yuki's mother now?
questions.e: Write the ages as 2x and 7x. In 10 years, (2x + 10)/(7x + 10) = 4/9, so 18x + 90 = 28x + 40 and x = 5. The mother is 7 × 5 = 35 (Yuki is 10). Check: in 10 years they are 20 and 45, and 20 : 45 = 4 : 9. Choosing 10 gives Yuki's age.

questions.s: The ages of three siblings add up to 51. The middle sibling is 3 years older than the youngest, and the eldest is twice as old as the youngest. How old is the eldest sibling?
questions.e: If the youngest is y, the ages are y, y + 3 and 2y, so 4y + 3 = 51 and y = 12. The eldest is 2 × 12 = 24. Stopping at y = 12 answers for the youngest instead of the eldest.

questions.s: A father is 30 years older than his son, who is now 9 years old. In how many years will the father be exactly 3 times as old as his son?
questions.e: The father is now 39. In t years, 39 + t = 3(9 + t), so 39 + t = 27 + 3t and t = 6. Check: the son will be 15 and the father 45. Note that the father is already more than 3 times as old as his son (39 > 27), so the answer must be a number of years in the future in which the ratio falls to 3.

questions.s: The average age of the 6 members of a string sextet is 28. When a seventh musician joins, the average age of the 7 musicians becomes 30. How old is the new musician?
questions.e: The six ages total 6 × 28 = 168, and the seven ages total 7 × 30 = 210, so the new musician is 210 − 168 = 42. Thinking the newcomer only needs to be 2 years above the old average (30) misses that the newcomer's extra years are shared among all 7 people.

questions.s: Ines is 4 years older than her brother Tomas. Their ages are positive whole numbers, and the product of their ages is less than 200. Which of the following could be Ines's age? Indicate all such ages.
questions.e: We need I(I − 4) < 200 with I − 4 ≥ 1. At I = 16 the product is 16 × 12 = 192, which works, but at I = 17 it is 17 × 13 = 221, which is too big. So 6, 12, 15 and 16 are possible. Taking √200 ≈ 14 as the limit for Ines is the trap: that would be the limit if both had the same age.

questions.s: Five years ago, Arjun was 3 times as old as his cousin Dev. In 5 years, Arjun will be twice as old as Dev. How old is Arjun now?
questions.e: From the two facts, A − 5 = 3(D − 5) and A + 5 = 2(D + 5), so A = 3D − 10 and A = 2D + 5. Then 3D − 10 = 2D + 5 gives D = 15 and A = 35. Check: 5 years ago they were 30 and 10; in 5 years they will be 40 and 20. The choice 15 is Dev's age.

questions.s: The ages of four cousins are consecutive odd integers, and the sum of their ages is 72. How old is the youngest cousin?
questions.e: Consecutive odd integers differ by 2: n, n + 2, n + 4, n + 6. Their sum 4n + 12 = 72 gives n = 15, so the ages are 15, 17, 19 and 21. The average age, 18, is not even one of the ages, and 21 is the oldest cousin.

questions.s: A gym in Melbourne charges 40 dollars for the first month of membership, and the fee rises by 2.50 dollars each month after that. What is the total amount a member pays for the first 12 months?
questions.e: The 12th month costs 40 + 11 × 2.50 = 67.50 dollars, so the total is 12 × (40 + 67.50)/2 = 6 × 107.50 = 645 dollars. Using 12 increases (a last fee of 70) gives 660, and forgetting to halve the sum of the first and last terms gives 1,290.

questions.s: A car bought for 24,000 dollars loses 15% of its value each year, with each year's loss based on its value at the start of that year. What is the car's value at the end of 3 years?
questions.e: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.85, so after 3 years it is 24,000 × 0.85³ = 24,000 × 0.614125 = 14,739 dollars. Taking 45% off the original price (13,200) treats the losses as all based on 24,000, and 17,340 is the value after only 2 years. 9,261 is the total loss.

questions.s: A lab culture starts with 3 cells. At the end of every hour, the number of cells doubles and then 1 cell is removed for testing. How many cells are in the culture right after the removal at the end of the 5th hour?
questions.e: Apply 'double, then subtract 1' five times: 3 → 5 → 9 → 17 → 33 → 65. Each value is one more than a power of 2 (2ⁿ⁺¹ + 1). Subtracting before doubling would give a different, smaller sequence (3 → 4 → 6 → 10 → 18 → 34).

questions.s: Amara runs 5 kilometers on the first day of her training plan and runs 0.5 kilometer more each day than the day before. On which day does she first run at least 12 kilometers?
questions.e: On day n she runs 5 + 0.5(n − 1) km. Setting this equal to 12 gives n − 1 = 14, so n = 15. Day 14 is the number of increases, not the day number; dividing 12 by 0.5 to get 24 ignores the 5 km starting distance.

questions.s: In a stadium, the numbers of seats in the rows form an arithmetic sequence, starting with row 1. Row 5 has 34 seats and row 12 has 55 seats. Which of the following could be the number of seats in some row of the stadium? Indicate all such numbers.
questions.e: From row 5 to row 12 is 7 steps and 21 seats, so each row has 3 more seats than the one before, and row 1 has 34 − 4 × 3 = 22. Possible counts are 22, 25, 28, ..., the numbers 22 or more that leave remainder 1 when divided by 3: 22, 46 (row 9) and 100 (row 27). 41 and 62 have the wrong remainder, and 19 would be row 0, which does not exist.

questions.s: A factory in Monterrey produces 1,200 units in its first month of operation, and each month after that it produces 50 more units than in the month before. In which month does its total production since opening first exceed 20,000 units?
questions.e: The total after n months is 1,200n + 50 × n(n − 1)/2 = 1,200n + 25n(n − 1). After 13 months it is 15,600 + 3,900 = 19,500, just short; after 14 months it is 16,800 + 4,550 = 21,350. So month 14 is the first. Dividing 20,000 by 1,200 (about 16.7, so month 17) ignores the growth.

questions.s: A car's fuel economy is 40 miles per gallon. Using 1 mile = 1.6 kilometers and 1 gallon = 3.8 liters, which of the following is closest to the car's fuel economy in kilometers per liter?
questions.e: Convert the numerator and the denominator: 40 miles = 64 km and 1 gallon = 3.8 liters, so the economy is 64/3.8 ≈ 16.8 km per liter. Dividing 40 by both factors (about 6.6) converts the miles the wrong way, and 95.0 comes from multiplying by 3.8 and dividing by 1.6.

questions.s: A shop sells fabric at 12 dollars per yard. A tailor needs 4.5 meters of the fabric. Using 1 yard = 0.9144 meter, how much will the fabric cost, to the nearest dollar?
questions.e: A meter is longer than a yard, so 4.5 meters is more than 4.5 yards: 4.5/0.9144 ≈ 4.92 yards. The cost is about 4.92 × 12 ≈ 59.06, or 59 dollars. Multiplying by 0.9144 instead (about 49 dollars) converts in the wrong direction.

questions.s: A rectangular water tank measures 2 meters by 1.5 meters by 0.8 meter. It is filled from empty at a rate of 12 liters per minute. How many hours does it take to fill the tank? (1 cubic meter = 1,000 liters)
questions.e: The volume is 2 × 1.5 × 0.8 = 2.4 cubic meters, or 2,400 liters. At 12 liters per minute this takes 200 minutes, which is 200/60 = 3 1/3 hours. Choosing 200 stops at minutes, and 33 1/3 comes from writing 2.4 cubic meters as 24,000 liters.

questions.s: Which of the following speeds are equal to 90 kilometers per hour? Indicate all such speeds.
questions.e: 90 km/h is 90,000 meters in 3,600 seconds, which is 25 m/s, and 90/60 = 1.5 km per minute (1,500 m per minute, not 150). In a day it covers 90 × 24 = 2,160 km. Since 25 m/s = 0.025 km per second, 0.25 km per second is ten times too fast.

questions.s: Before a trip to Japan, Sofia exchanges 800 dollars for yen at a rate of 150 yen per dollar. She spends 90,000 yen during the trip and, on returning, exchanges the remaining yen back into dollars at a rate of 160 yen per dollar. How many dollars does she get back?
questions.e: She receives 800 × 150 = 120,000 yen and has 120,000 − 90,000 = 30,000 yen left. At 160 yen per dollar that is 30,000/160 = 187.50 dollars. Using the original rate of 150 gives 200 dollars, and 562.50 converts the yen she spent instead of the yen she kept.

questions.s: A bread recipe for 6 servings uses 450 grams of flour. Kenji wants to make 10 servings and measures flour in cups, where 1 cup of this flour weighs 125 grams. How many cups of flour does he need?
questions.e: Scaling up, 10 servings need 450 × 10/6 = 750 grams, which is 750/125 = 6 cups. Converting the original 450 grams (3.6 cups) forgets the scaling, and 2.16 scales by 6/10 instead of 10/6.

questions.s: A retailer marks up the cost of a phone by p percent and then sells it at a 10% discount off the marked price. If the retailer's profit is at least 8% and at most 17% of the cost, which of the following could be p? Indicate all such values.
questions.e: The selling price is 0.9(1 + p/100) times the cost, and it must be between 1.08 and 1.17 times the cost. Dividing by 0.9 gives 1.20 ≤ 1 + p/100 ≤ 1.30, so 20 ≤ p ≤ 30. Adding 10 to the profit range (18% to 27%) is the trap; it ignores that the discount is a percent of the larger marked price.

questions.s: A truck driver covers a route at a constant speed. If she drove 10 kilometers per hour faster, the trip would take 1 hour less; if she drove 10 kilometers per hour slower, it would take 1.5 hours more. How long is the route, in kilometers?
questions.e: With speed v and distance d, d/v − d/(v + 10) = 1 gives 10d = v(v + 10), and d/(v − 10) − d/v = 1.5 gives 10d = 1.5v(v − 10). Setting these equal, v + 10 = 1.5(v − 10), so v = 50 and d = 50 × 60/10 = 300 km. Check: 6 hours at 50, 5 hours at 60 and 7.5 hours at 40.

questions.s: Mateo drives the first half of the distance from Porto to Madrid at an average of 40 kilometers per hour because of road works. At what average speed, in kilometers per hour, must he drive the second half so that his average speed for the whole trip is 48 kilometers per hour?
questions.e: Take a half-distance of 240 km. At 48 km/h the 480 km trip must take 10 hours, and the first half takes 240/40 = 6 hours, leaving 4 hours for 240 km: 60 km/h. The tempting 56 assumes the average of 40 and the second speed is 48, but equal distances are not equal times, so the slower half counts for more.

questions.s: Two runners start at the same point on a 400-meter circular track and run in opposite directions at constant speeds of 3.5 and 4.5 meters per second. How many times do they pass each other during the first 11 minutes, not counting the start?
questions.e: Running in opposite directions, together they cover 3.5 + 4.5 = 8 meters every second, and they meet each time their combined distance grows by a full lap of 400 m: every 50 seconds. In 11 minutes = 660 seconds that happens 660/50 = 13.2 times, so 13 full meetings. Using the difference of the speeds (1 m/s) would describe runners going the same way.

questions.s: A train traveling at a constant speed passes a signal pole in 12 seconds and passes completely through a 300-meter tunnel in 27 seconds, measured from the moment its front enters the tunnel until its rear leaves it. Which of the following statements are true? Indicate all such statements.
questions.e: Passing the pole, the train covers its own length L in 12 s; passing the tunnel, it covers L + 300 in 27 s. So 300 m takes 15 s, the speed is 20 m/s (72 km/h) and L = 240 m. Crossing a 300-m bridge also means covering L + 300, which takes 27 s, not 15 s. Two such trains approach at 40 m/s and must cover 480 m together, which takes 12 s.
o: The train's speed is 72 kilometers per hour.
The train takes 15 seconds to cross a 300-meter bridge completely.
Two trains of this length and speed, on parallel tracks in opposite directions, take 12 seconds to pass each other completely.

questions.s: A boat travels 24 kilometers downstream and then returns 24 kilometers upstream on a river whose current flows at 2 kilometers per hour. The round trip takes 5 hours of travel. What is the boat's speed in still water, in kilometers per hour?
questions.e: With still-water speed b, the times are 24/(b + 2) + 24/(b − 2) = 5, which simplifies to 5b² − 48b − 20 = 0, so b = 10 (the other root is negative). Check: 24/12 + 24/8 = 2 + 3 = 5 hours. The choice 9.6 is the average speed 48/5, which ignores the current's unequal effect on the two legs.

questions.s: Working together, pumps A and B can drain a flooded basement in 12 hours. Pump A alone would take 10 hours less than pump B alone. How many hours would pump B alone take?
questions.e: If B takes x hours, A takes x − 10, and 1/x + 1/(x − 10) = 1/12. Clearing denominators gives x² − 34x + 120 = 0, so x = 30 or x = 4; x = 4 is impossible because A's time would be negative. So B takes 30 hours and A 20 (check: 1/30 + 1/20 = 1/12). The choice 20 is pump A's time.

questions.s: Kenji can paint a mural alone in 9 days, and Lina can paint it alone in 6 days. They take turns working on the mural on alternate days, with Kenji working on the first day. How many days does it take to finish the mural?
questions.e: Each two-day pair finishes 1/9 + 1/6 = 5/18 of the mural, so after 6 days 15/18 is done. Kenji's 7th day brings it to 17/18, and Lina needs only 1/18 ÷ 1/6 = 1/3 of day 8, for 7 1/3 days. The choice 7.2 doubles the 3.6 days they would need working together, which assumes the job ends exactly at the end of a pair of days.

questions.s: A crew of 12 workers, each working 8 hours a day, finishes a paving job in 15 days. A second job is 1.5 times as large. How many days will 18 workers take to finish the second job if each works 10 hours a day at the same hourly rate?
questions.e: The first job takes 12 × 15 × 8 = 1,440 worker-hours, so the second needs 1.5 × 1,440 = 2,160. The new crew supplies 18 × 10 = 180 worker-hours per day, so it needs 2,160/180 = 12 days. Forgetting the larger size of the second job gives 8 days.

questions.s: Machines A and B together can complete a job in 6 hours, machines B and C together in 10 hours, and machines A and C together in 7.5 hours. Each machine works at its own constant rate. Which of the following statements are true? Indicate all such statements.
questions.e: Add the three pair rates: 1/6 + 1/10 + 2/15 = 2/5, which counts each machine twice, so all three together work at 1/5 job per hour (5 hours). Then A = 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10 (10 hours), B = 1/5 − 2/15 = 1/15 (15 hours) and C = 1/5 − 1/6 = 1/30 (30 hours). B takes 15 hours, not 12, and A is 1.5 times as fast as B, not twice.
o: Machine B alone would take 12 hours.
All three machines together would take 5 hours.
Machine A works twice as fast as machine B.
Machine C alone would take 30 hours.
Machine A alone would take 10 hours.

questions.s: A tank has two inlet pipes and a leak. Inlet A alone fills the empty tank in 3 hours, inlet B alone fills it in 5 hours, and the leak alone empties a full tank in 15 hours. The tank starts empty with both inlets open and the leak active, and inlet A is closed after 1 hour. How many hours after the start is the tank full?
questions.e: In the first hour the tank gains 1/3 + 1/5 − 1/15 = 7/15. After A is closed it gains 1/5 − 1/15 = 2/15 per hour, so the remaining 8/15 takes 4 hours, for a total of 5 hours. The choice 4 forgets the first hour, and 2 1/7 is the time if A stayed open throughout.

questions.s: Jug P contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1, and jug Q contains milk and water in the ratio 5 : 3. In what ratio should liquid from P and liquid from Q be mixed to obtain a mixture that is milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1?
questions.e: Milk is 3/4 of P, 5/8 of Q and must be 2/3 of the mixture. With p parts of P and q parts of Q, (3/4)p + (5/8)q = (2/3)(p + q), so (1/12)p = (1/24)q and p : q = 1 : 2. The target 2/3 is closer to Q's 5/8, so more of Q is needed; 2 : 1 reverses the ratio.

questions.s: A farm in Sicily dries 60 kilograms of fresh tomatoes that are 94% water by weight. After drying, the tomatoes are 25% water by weight. What is the weight of the dried tomatoes, in kilograms?
questions.e: Only water evaporates, so the 6% of solids, 0.06 × 60 = 3.6 kg, stays. After drying, those solids are 75% of the weight, so the dried tomatoes weigh 3.6/0.75 = 4.8 kg. Taking 25% of 60 (15 kg) or subtracting 94 − 25 = 69 percentage points of the weight (18.6 kg) treats the percents as if the total weight stayed the same.

questions.s: A barrel holds 80 liters of olive oil. A certain amount is drawn off and replaced with a cheaper oil, and the mixture is stirred. The same amount of mixture is then drawn off and again replaced with the cheaper oil. The barrel now contains 45 liters of the original olive oil. How many liters were drawn off each time?
questions.e: Each replacement keeps the fraction (1 − x/80) of the original oil, so 80(1 − x/80)² = 45, (1 − x/80)² = 9/16 and 1 − x/80 = 3/4, giving x = 20. Splitting the 35-liter drop evenly (17.5 liters each time) fails because the second draw contains some cheaper oil, so it removes less of the original.
